Appendicitis
questions.why: The narrow, worm-like tube attached to the cecum is the vermiform appendix, a tube of lymphatic tissue. The cecum sits in the lower right part of the abdomen, so inflammation of the appendix, called appendicitis, brings pain there. If the inflamed appendix ruptures, infection can spread to the peritoneum.
notes: Colorectal cancer is a malignant tumor of the colon or rectum, not inflammation of the appendix. It would be the answer for a question about a tumor of the large intestine.
Gastroesophageal reflux disease is backflow of stomach contents into the esophagus, felt as heartburn behind the breastbone. Pick it for a weak lower esophageal sphincter, not for pain at the cecum.
A peptic ulcer is an eroded sore in the wall of the stomach or duodenum, which lie in the upper abdomen. Choose it for a question about a sore in the stomach lining.
Correct. Inflammation of the vermiform appendix is appendicitis.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which disorder is chronic inflammation of the intestinal wall and includes Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis?
options: Hemorrhoids
Peptic ulcer
Diverticulosis
Inflammatory bowel disease
questions.why: Inflammatory bowel disease is a group of disorders marked by long-lasting (chronic) inflammation of the intestinal wall. Its two main forms are Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. The word bowel refers to the intestines, which is where this inflammation is found.
notes: Hemorrhoids are swollen, dilated veins in the wall of the anal canal and rectum. Choose them if the question described swollen veins near the anus.
A peptic ulcer is an eroded sore in the wall of the stomach or duodenum. It would be the answer for a single sore in the upper digestive tract.
Diverticulosis is small pouches bulging outward through weak spots in the colon wall, a structural change rather than chronic inflammation. Pick it if the question described pouches in the colon.
Correct. Inflammatory bowel disease includes Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A region of the stomach narrows like a funnel and connects the body of the stomach to the duodenum. Which region is it?
options: The fundus
The pyloric part
The cardia
The body
questions.why: The pyloric part is the exit region of the stomach. It narrows from the wide pyloric antrum through the pyloric canal to the pylorus, which is guarded by the pyloric sphincter where the stomach meets the duodenum. Its funnel shape guides the liquefied stomach contents toward the small intestine.
notes: The fundus is the rounded portion that bulges above and to the left of the cardia. It would be the answer if the question asked for the dome-shaped top of the stomach.
Correct. The pyloric part narrows and connects the body of the stomach to the duodenum.
The cardia surrounds the opening from the esophagus, at the entrance end of the stomach. Pick it if the question asked where food enters the stomach.
The body is the large central portion of the stomach, between the fundus and the pyloric part. Choose it if the question asked for the biggest region of the stomach.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which region of the small intestine is the last and longest, joining the large intestine at the ileocecal sphincter?
options: The duodenum
The cecum
The jejunum
The ileum
questions.why: The ileum is the final region of the small intestine and also the longest, about 2 m (6 feet). It ends at the ileocecal sphincter, a thickening of smooth muscle where it opens into the cecum of the large intestine, and together with folds of mucosa this sphincter forms the ileocecal valve. The spelling helps: the ileum of the intestine is different from the ilium of the hip bone.
notes: The duodenum is the first and shortest region, about 25 cm (10 inches), starting at the pyloric sphincter. Pick it if the question asked where the small intestine begins.

The cecum is the pouch at the start of the large intestine, on the far side of the ileocecal sphincter, so it is not part of the small intestine. Choose it if the question asked what the ileum empties into.
The jejunum is the middle region, about 1 m (3 feet) long. It would be the answer if the question asked which region lies between the duodenum and the ileum.
Correct. The ileum is the last and longest region and joins the large intestine at the ileocecal sphincter.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which surface feature of the small intestine is a permanent circular ridge of the mucosa and submucosa?
options: Rugae
Microvilli
Villi
Circular folds
questions.why: The circular folds, or plicae circulares, are the largest of the small intestine's three surface features. They are permanent ridges that involve both the mucosa and the submucosa, so they do not flatten out when the intestine fills. Villi project from the folds, and microvilli cover the cells of each villus, so the surface is increased three times over.
notes: Rugae are folds of the stomach lining, and unlike the circular folds they flatten out as the stomach fills. Choose rugae for a question about the stomach.
Microvilli are microscopic projections of single absorptive cells that form the brush border. They would be the answer for the smallest of the three surface features.

Villi are finger-like projections of the mucosa only, smaller than the circular folds and sitting on top of them. Pick villi if the question asked about the projections that give the lining a velvety look.
Correct. The circular folds are permanent ridges of the mucosa and submucosa.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which region of the large intestine is the straight portion lying anterior to the sacrum and coccyx?
options: The sigmoid colon
The rectum
The anal canal
The cecum
questions.why: The rectum is the straight portion of the large intestine, running down in the pelvis in front of the sacrum and coccyx. Its name comes from the Latin word for straight. It follows the sigmoid colon and stores feces before they pass into the anal canal.
notes: The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped last part of the colon, just before the rectum. Its curves set it apart from the straight rectum. Pick it if the question asked which segment of the colon leads into the rectum.
Correct. The rectum is the straight portion anterior to the sacrum and coccyx.
The anal canal is the last few centimeters of the tract, after the rectum, ending at the anus. It would be the answer if the question asked for the final short segment of the canal.
The cecum is the pouch at the start of the large intestine, in the lower right abdomen, far from the sacrum. Choose it if the question asked where the large intestine begins.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which feature of the colon is a series of pouches formed by the pull of the teniae coli?
options: Rugae
Circular folds
Haustra
Villi
questions.why: Haustra are the pouches that give the colon its puckered appearance. The three teniae coli, bands of longitudinal muscle, are shorter than the colon wall and gather it into a row of sacs. Haustra, teniae coli, and omental appendices together identify the large intestine.
notes: Rugae are folds of the stomach lining that flatten as the stomach fills. They would be the answer for a question about the stomach.
Circular folds are permanent ridges of the mucosa and submucosa in the small intestine. Choose them for the largest surface feature of the small intestine.
Correct. Haustra are the pouches of the colon formed by the teniae coli.
Villi are finger-like projections of the small intestine mucosa that increase surface area for absorption. Pick villi for a question about the small intestine lining.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which disorder is an eroded sore in the wall of the stomach or duodenum?
options: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
Appendicitis
Peptic ulcer
Diverticulosis
questions.why: A peptic ulcer is an eroded sore in the wall of the stomach or the duodenum, the regions exposed to stomach acid. It begins in the mucosa, and the danger is that it erodes deeper through the submucosa and muscularis. If it perforates the serosa, the contents of the lumen spill into the peritoneal cavity.
notes: Gastroesophageal reflux disease is backflow of stomach contents into the esophagus through a weak lower esophageal sphincter, not a sore in the stomach. Pick it for a question about heartburn from reflux.
Appendicitis is inflammation of the vermiform appendix attached to the cecum. Choose it for a question about pain in the lower right abdomen.
Correct. A peptic ulcer is an eroded sore in the stomach or duodenal wall.
Diverticulosis is small pouches bulging outward through weak spots in the colon wall. It would be the answer for a question about the large intestine wall.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which disorder is small pouches bulging outward through weak spots in the colon wall?
options: Colorectal cancer
Hiatal hernia
Diverticulosis
Inflammatory bowel disease
questions.why: Diverticulosis is the presence of small pouches, called diverticula, that bulge outward through weak spots in the colon wall. It is a change in the structure of the wall rather than an inflammation or tumor. It is different from the haustra, which are the normal pouches of the colon formed by the teniae coli.
notes: Colorectal cancer is a malignant tumor of the colon or rectum. It would be the answer for a question about a tumor rather than pouches.
A hiatal hernia is part of the stomach pushing up through the esophageal hiatus of the diaphragm. Choose it for a question about the stomach and diaphragm.
Correct. Diverticulosis is small pouches bulging through weak spots in the colon wall.

Inflammatory bowel disease is chronic inflammation of the intestinal wall, as in Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis, not outward pouches. Pick it if the question described long-lasting inflammation of the intestine.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which region of the small intestine is the middle region, about 1 m (3 feet) long?
options: The colon
The jejunum
The ileum
The duodenum
questions.why: The small intestine runs duodenum, jejunum, then ileum. The jejunum is the middle region, about 1 m (3 feet) long, lying between the short duodenum (about 25 cm, or 10 inches) and the long ileum (about 2 m, or 6 feet). Along with the ileum, it hangs within the peritoneal cavity on the mesentery.
notes: The colon is part of the large intestine, not the small intestine. Choose it if the question asked about the ascending, transverse, descending, and sigmoid segments.
Correct. The jejunum is the middle region of the small intestine.
The ileum is the last and longest region, about 2 m (6 feet). It would be the answer if the question asked which region joins the large intestine.
The duodenum is the first and shortest region, about 25 cm (10 inches). Pick it if the question asked which region starts at the pyloric sphincter.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The stomach has a short concave medial border and a long convex lateral border. What are these two borders called?
options: The cardia and the pylorus
The fundus and the body
The pyloric antrum and pyloric canal
The lesser and greater curvatures
questions.why: The stomach is J-shaped, so it has two curved borders. The lesser curvature is the short, concave border on the right (medial) side, facing the liver, and the greater curvature is the long, convex border on the left (lateral) side. The lesser omentum attaches along the lesser curvature, and the greater omentum hangs from the greater curvature.
notes: The cardia and pylorus are the entrance and exit regions of the stomach, not its borders. Pick them if the question asked where food enters and leaves the stomach.
The fundus and body are regions of the stomach, the dome on top and the large central portion. They would be the answer for a question about the upper and central regions.
The pyloric antrum and pyloric canal are subdivisions of the pyloric part of the stomach. Choose them if the question asked what makes up the funnel leading to the pylorus.
Correct. The lesser curvature is the short concave medial border and the greater curvature is the long convex lateral border.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence correctly orders these organs as food travels through the canal: esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine?
options: Esophagus, small intestine, stomach, large intestine
Stomach, esophagus, small intestine, large intestine
Esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Esophagus, stomach, large intestine, small intestine
questions.why: Food moves through the canal in one direction. The esophagus carries it to the stomach, where it is churned into a liquid. It then passes into the small intestine, where most absorption happens, and finally into the large intestine, where water is absorbed and feces form.
notes: This puts the small intestine before the stomach. The stomach empties through the pyloric sphincter into the duodenum, so the stomach must come before the small intestine.
This puts the stomach before the esophagus. The esophagus is the tube that delivers food to the stomach, so it must come first.
Correct. Food travels from the esophagus to the stomach, then the small intestine, then the large intestine.

This puts the large intestine before the small intestine. Students sometimes order them by the word large, but the small intestine always comes first, and the large intestine is the final, wider region.
questions.answerText: Esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence correctly orders the regions of the small intestine as food moves through it, followed by the structure the ileum empties into?
options: Duodenum, jejunum, ileum, then the rectum
Duodenum, jejunum, ileum, then the cecum
Jejunum, duodenum, ileum, then the cecum
Duodenum, ileum, jejunum, then the cecum
questions.why: The small intestine runs duodenum, jejunum, then ileum. The ileum empties through the ileocecal valve into the cecum, the pouch at the start of the large intestine. From the cecum, material moves through the colon and only later reaches the rectum.
notes: The rectum is near the end of the large intestine, after the whole colon, so the ileum does not empty into it. The rectum would be the answer for where the sigmoid colon leads.
Correct. Food passes the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum, then enters the cecum.
This puts the jejunum first, but the duodenum is the first region, starting right at the pyloric sphincter.
This swaps the jejunum and ileum. The jejunum is the middle region, and the ileum is the last and longest region, the one that reaches the large intestine.
questions.answerText: Duodenum, jejunum, ileum, then the cecum

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence correctly orders the four parts of the colon as material travels through it?
options: Ascending, transverse, sigmoid, descending
Ascending, transverse, descending, sigmoid
Transverse, ascending, descending, sigmoid
Ascending, descending, transverse, sigmoid
questions.why: The colon frames the small intestine on three sides. Material rises from the cecum up the right side in the ascending colon, turns at the hepatic flexure to cross in the transverse colon, turns at the splenic flexure to drop down the left side in the descending colon, and then curves through the S-shaped sigmoid colon into the rectum.
notes: This puts the sigmoid colon before the descending colon. The sigmoid colon is the last part, connecting the descending colon to the rectum.
Correct. The colon runs ascending, transverse, descending, then sigmoid.
This puts the transverse colon first, but the colon starts by rising from the cecum on the right, so the ascending colon is first.
This puts the descending colon before the transverse colon. The colon has to cross the abdomen before it can descend on the left side, so the transverse colon comes second.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces the end of the canal, from the straight segment that holds feces, to the short terminal segment, to the exit?
options: Rectum, cecum, anus
Rectum, anal canal, anus
Anal canal, rectum, anus
Sigmoid colon, rectum, anus
questions.why: The final stretch of the canal begins with the rectum, the straight portion anterior to the sacrum and coccyx that stores feces. Next comes the anal canal, the last few centimeters of the tract, which passes through the pelvic floor. It ends at the anus, the exit, and the internal and external anal sphincters surround the anal canal.
notes: The cecum is the pouch at the start of the large intestine, not near its end. It would be the answer for where the ileum empties.
Correct. The rectum, anal canal, and anus form the end of the canal in that order.
This swaps the rectum and the anal canal. The rectum comes first, and the anal canal is the short final segment that ends at the anus.

The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped part just before the rectum, so this sequence starts one step too early and skips the anal canal. Pick the sigmoid colon if the question asked what leads into the rectum.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence names the three surface features that expand the absorptive surface of the small intestine, from largest to smallest?
options: Microvilli, villi, circular folds
Circular folds, villi, microvilli
Circular folds, rugae, microvilli
Villi, circular folds, microvilli
questions.why: The small intestine increases its surface three times over, each feature smaller than the last. The circular folds (plicae circulares) are permanent ridges of the mucosa and submucosa. Villi are finger-like projections of the mucosa that stand on those folds. Microvilli are microscopic projections of the single absorptive cells covering each villus, forming the brush border.
notes: This is the correct list run backward, from smallest to largest. It would be right only if the question asked for the order starting with the smallest feature.
Correct. Circular folds hold villi, and villi are covered by cells with microvilli.
Rugae are folds of the stomach lining, not a feature of the small intestine. They would be the answer for a question about how the stomach expands to hold a meal.
This puts the villi first, but villi are projections of the mucosa that sit on top of the much larger circular folds of the wall.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which list names only organs of the alimentary canal itself, the tube that food passes through?
options: The pharynx, esophagus, stomach, pancreas, small intestine, and large intestine
The mouth, esophagus, stomach, liver, small intestine, and large intestine
The teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas
The mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine
questions.why: The organs of the alimentary canal are the ones food actually travels through: the mouth, the pharynx, the esophagus, the stomach, and the small and large intestines. The accessory organs sit alongside the tube and send their secretions into it, but food never passes through them. The liver and pancreas, for example, empty bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum.
notes: This list slips in the pancreas, an accessory organ that empties pancreatic juice into the duodenum. Food never travels through the pancreas.
This list slips in the liver, an accessory organ that makes bile and sends it to the duodenum through ducts. Food never travels through the liver.
These are the accessory digestive organs, which help digestion without being part of the tube. Pick this list if the question asked for the accessory organs.
Correct. Food passes through each of these organs in turn.
questions.answerText: The mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which structure is the narrow, worm-like tube of lymphatic tissue attached to the cecum?
options: The ileum
The vermiform appendix
The palatine tonsil
The sigmoid colon
questions.why: The vermiform appendix is a narrow tube attached to the cecum, and vermiform means worm-shaped. Its wall is rich in lymphatic tissue, so it belongs to the immune defenses of the gut. When it becomes inflamed, the condition is appendicitis.
notes: The ileum is the last region of the small intestine, which opens into the cecum at the ileocecal valve rather than hanging from it. Choose it if the question asked which region joins the large intestine.
Correct. The vermiform appendix is the worm-like lymphatic tube attached to the cecum.

The palatine tonsil is also lymphatic tissue, but it sits between the palatal arches at the back of the mouth, not on the cecum. Pick it if the question asked about lymphatic tissue guarding the oropharynx.
The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped last part of the colon, leading into the rectum. It would be the answer if the question asked which colon segment is curved like an S.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: How many layers of smooth muscle are in the muscularis of the stomach?
options: Four
Three
One
Two
questions.why: The stomach muscularis has three layers of smooth muscle: an inner oblique layer, a middle circular layer, and an outer longitudinal layer. That is one more layer than the rest of the canal, which usually has only the circular and longitudinal layers. The extra oblique layer lets the stomach churn food as well as push it.
notes: Four is the number of tunics in the canal wall (mucosa, submucosa, muscularis, serosa), not the number of muscle layers. Students often carry that number over by mistake.
Correct. The stomach has three smooth muscle layers in its muscularis.
One layer is too few for any part of the muscularis. A single thin layer of smooth muscle does exist in the mucosa, the muscularis mucosae, which may be the source of this mix-up.
Two layers, inner circular and outer longitudinal, is the usual count for the rest of the canal. Pick two if the question asked about the muscularis of the small intestine or colon.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which structure inside each villus is a lymphatic capillary that absorbs dietary fats?
options: A blood capillary
A gastric pit
A microvillus
The lacteal
questions.why: Each villus contains a lacteal, a lymphatic capillary in its core. Dietary fats are absorbed into the lacteal and travel in the lymph rather than going straight into the blood. Its name comes from the milky look of the fat-filled lymph after a meal.
notes: Villi also hold blood capillaries, which take up most other absorbed nutrients, but they are part of the blood system, not the lymphatic system. Pick a blood capillary if the question asked where sugars and amino acids enter the villus.
A gastric pit is an opening in the stomach lining that leads to the gastric glands, not a structure inside a villus. It would be the answer for a question about the stomach lining.
A microvillus is a microscopic projection on the surface of an absorptive cell, part of the brush border, not a vessel inside the villus. Choose it if the question asked what forms the brush border.
Correct. The lacteal is the lymphatic capillary in each villus that absorbs dietary fats.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Imaging shows part of a patient's stomach pushed up through the opening in the diaphragm that the esophagus passes through. Which disorder is this, and which opening is involved?
options: An inguinal hernia, through the esophageal hiatus
A hiatal hernia, through the pyloric sphincter
A hiatal hernia, through the esophageal hiatus
Gastroesophageal reflux disease, through the pyloric canal
questions.why: The esophagus passes from the thorax into the abdomen through an opening in the diaphragm called the esophageal hiatus. In a hiatal hernia, part of the stomach pushes up through that same opening into the thorax. The word hiatal comes from hiatus, which names the opening involved.
notes: The opening is right, but an inguinal hernia is a different disorder, in which intestine pushes through the inguinal canal in the groin. Choose an inguinal hernia for a bulge in the groin.

The disorder is right, but the pyloric sphincter is the ring of muscle between the stomach and duodenum, not an opening in the diaphragm. The pyloric sphincter would be the answer for where food leaves the stomach.
Correct. A hiatal hernia is the stomach pushing up through the esophageal hiatus.

Gastroesophageal reflux disease is backflow of stomach contents through a weak lower esophageal sphincter, not the stomach moving through the diaphragm, and the pyloric canal is at the stomach's exit. Pick GERD for heartburn from reflux.
questions.answerText: A hiatal hernia, through the esophageal hiatus

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The small intestine is lined with villi, and each villus is covered in cells bearing microvilli. Why does this lining suit the small intestine's main job?
options: It greatly increases the surface area for absorbing nutrients
It adds a muscle layer that churns and mixes the contents
It lets the small intestine stretch to store a large meal
It forms pouches that hold waste while water is absorbed
questions.why: The small intestine is where most absorption happens, and absorption depends on how much lining the digested food can touch. Villi multiply the surface of the mucosa, and the microvilli on each absorptive cell multiply it again. Along with the circular folds, these features give the small intestine an enormous absorptive surface packed into a tube that fits in the abdomen.
notes: Correct. Villi and microvilli greatly increase the surface area for absorption.

An extra muscle layer that churns food is the oblique layer of the stomach's muscularis. Villi and microvilli are part of the mucosa and contain no extra muscle layer. Choose this for a question about the stomach muscularis.
Stretching to store a meal is the job of the stomach, whose rugae flatten as it fills. Pick this for a question about rugae.
Pouches that hold waste while water is absorbed describe the haustra of the colon. This would be the answer for a question about the large intestine.
questions.answerText: It greatly increases the surface area for absorbing nutrients

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The stomach lining is folded into rugae and coated with a thick layer of mucus. Which statement best explains why each feature matters to the stomach?
options: The rugae anchor the stomach to the liver, and the mucus fills the peritoneal cavity
The rugae let the stomach expand with a meal, and the mucus shields the lining from the stomach's own acid
The rugae are permanent ridges that slow food, and the mucus speeds absorption
The rugae squeeze food toward the duodenum, and the mucus breaks food down
questions.why: The stomach works as a holding reservoir and a mixing chamber full of strong acid. The rugae are folds of the lining that flatten out as a meal arrives, so the stomach can stretch to hold it. The thick mucus coats the lining so the acid works on the food rather than on the stomach wall itself. When that protection breaks down, a peptic ulcer can form.
notes: Anchoring the stomach to the liver is the job of the lesser omentum, and the slim fluid in the peritoneal cavity comes from the serous membrane, not stomach mucus. Choose the lesser omentum for a question about that attachment.
Correct. The rugae allow expansion, and the mucus protects the lining from acid.

Permanent ridges that slow the contents are the circular folds of the small intestine. Rugae are not permanent, since they flatten as the stomach fills. This would fit a question about the small intestine wall.

Squeezing food forward is the job of the muscularis, the smooth muscle tunic, not the folds of the lining, and mucus protects rather than digests. Pick the muscularis for a question about what moves stomach contents.
questions.answerText: The rugae let the stomach expand with a meal, and the mucus shields the lining from the stomach's own acid

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The small intestine absorbs most nutrients, while the large intestine mainly absorbs water and forms feces. Which statement best explains this division of labor?
options: Bile enters the large intestine and blocks nutrient absorption there
The large intestine has more villi than the small intestine, which suits it to water
The large intestine adds water to the waste to soften it before elimination
Most nutrients are already absorbed upstream, so what reaches the large intestine is mostly water and indigestible waste
questions.why: Food passes through the small intestine first, and its huge absorptive surface takes up most of the nutrients along the way. What enters the large intestine through the ileocecal valve is largely water and indigestible material. The large intestine reclaims much of that water and compacts what is left into feces, which the rectum holds until elimination.
notes: Bile enters the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla, at the start of the small intestine, not the large intestine. Pick the duodenum for a question about where bile and pancreatic juice enter the canal.

The large intestine lacks villi entirely, which is one way to tell it from the small intestine on a slide. Villi belong to the small intestine, so this would be the answer only in a question about the small intestine's absorptive surface.
The large intestine removes water from the waste rather than adding it, which is why feces become more solid as they move along the colon. This mix-up reverses the large intestine's real role.
Correct. The small intestine absorbs most nutrients first, leaving water and waste for the large intestine.
questions.answerText: Most nutrients are already absorbed upstream, so what reaches the large intestine is mostly water and indigestible waste

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The pyloric sphincter sits between the stomach and the duodenum. What is its job?
options: It lets the liquefied stomach contents into the duodenum a little at a time
It keeps material in the large intestine from flowing back into the ileum
It controls when feces leave the body through the anus
It keeps stomach contents from flowing back into the esophagus
questions.why: In the stomach, food is churned and held until it becomes a liquid. The pyloric sphincter, a ring of smooth muscle between the pylorus and the duodenum, opens to release that liquid into the small intestine in small amounts. This metering keeps the duodenum from being flooded so the small intestine can process each portion.
notes: Correct. The pyloric sphincter meters stomach contents into the duodenum.
Limiting backflow from the large intestine into the ileum is the job of the ileocecal valve. It would be the answer for a question about the junction of the small and large intestines.
Controlling when feces leave the body is the job of the internal and external anal sphincters at the end of the canal. Choose them for a question about the anus.
Keeping stomach contents out of the esophagus is the job of the lower esophageal sphincter at the stomach's entrance. Pick it for a question about reflux or GERD.
questions.answerText: It lets the liquefied stomach contents into the duodenum a little at a time

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the internal and external anal sphincters?
options: Both anal sphincters are voluntary skeletal muscle
Both anal sphincters are involuntary smooth muscle
The internal anal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle; the external anal sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle
The internal anal sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle; the external anal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle
questions.why: Two sphincters guard the anus. The internal anal sphincter is a thickening of the smooth muscle of the canal wall, so it is involuntary and works without conscious control. The external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle, so it is voluntary and lets a person decide when to release feces. Having one of each gives both automatic and conscious control.
notes: The external sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle, but the internal sphincter is smooth muscle like the rest of the canal wall. This mix-up comes from assuming both sphincters at one exit must be the same tissue.

The internal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle, but the external sphincter is skeletal muscle that you control at will. If both were involuntary, there would be no conscious control over elimination.
Correct. The internal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle and the external sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle.
This swaps the two. The internal sphincter is a continuation of the gut's own smooth muscle, which is involuntary, while the external one is skeletal muscle under conscious control.
questions.answerText: The internal anal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle; the external anal sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: What are the small fat-filled pouches of peritoneum that hang from the surface of the colon, mostly along the teniae coli?
options: Omental appendices
Lacteals
Diverticula
Haustra
questions.why: Omental appendices, also called epiploic appendages, are small fat-filled pouches of visceral peritoneum that hang from the surface of the colon, mostly along the teniae coli. Along with the teniae coli and the haustra, they are one of the three features found only on the large intestine, so they help you identify the colon on a model.
notes: Correct. Omental appendices are the fat-filled pouches of peritoneum on the surface of the colon.
Lacteals are lymphatic capillaries inside the villi of the small intestine that absorb dietary fats. Choose them for a question about fat absorption, not for structures on the colon surface.
Diverticula are abnormal pouches that bulge outward through weak spots in the colon wall, the defining feature of diverticulosis. They would be the answer for a question about that disorder.
Haustra are the pouches of the colon wall itself, formed by the pull of the teniae coli, and they are not filled with fat. Pick haustra if the question asked what gives the colon its puckered look.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which bend of the colon lies near the liver, where the ascending colon turns to become the transverse colon?
options: The sigmoid colon
The splenic flexure
The hepatic flexure
The ileocecal valve
questions.why: As the ascending colon rises on the right side of the abdomen, it reaches the underside of the liver and turns to run across the abdomen as the transverse colon. This bend is the hepatic flexure, also called the right colic flexure, named for the liver (hepatic). The matching bend on the left, near the spleen, is the splenic flexure.
notes: The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped last part of the colon, low in the pelvis, leading into the rectum. It would be the answer for the colon segment just before the rectum.

The splenic flexure, or left colic flexure, is the bend near the spleen where the transverse colon turns down to become the descending colon. Pick it if the question asked about the bend on the left side.
Correct. The hepatic flexure is the bend near the liver between the ascending and transverse colon.
The ileocecal valve is where the ileum opens into the cecum, at the very start of the large intestine, below the ascending colon. Choose it for the junction of the small and large intestines.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which disorder of the canal is swollen, dilated veins in the wall of the anal canal and rectum?
options: Inflammatory bowel disease
Diverticulosis
Colorectal cancer
Hemorrhoids
questions.why: Hemorrhoids are veins in the wall of the anal canal and rectum that have become swollen and dilated. They are a vascular problem, much like varicose veins elsewhere in the body, rather than a problem of the intestinal lining or muscle. Their location at the end of the canal explains why they are felt near the anus.
notes: Inflammatory bowel disease is chronic inflammation of the intestinal wall, as in Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. Choose it for long-lasting inflammation of the intestine.
Diverticulosis is small pouches bulging outward through weak spots in the colon wall, not swollen veins. Pick it for a question about pouches in the colon.
Colorectal cancer is a malignant tumor of the colon or rectum. It would be the answer for a question about a tumor rather than dilated veins.
Correct. Hemorrhoids are swollen, dilated veins of the anal canal and rectum.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: To which part of the large intestine is the vermiform appendix attached?
options: The cecum
The ileum
The sigmoid colon
The transverse colon
questions.why: The cecum is the pouch at the very start of the large intestine, just below the ileocecal valve in the lower right abdomen. The vermiform appendix, a narrow worm-shaped tube of lymphatic tissue, hangs from the cecum. That is why appendicitis causes pain in the lower right quadrant.
notes: Correct. The appendix hangs from the cecum.
The ileum is the last part of the small intestine, not the large intestine. It joins the cecum at the ileocecal valve, so it would be the answer for the segment that empties into the cecum.
The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped last part of the colon in the lower left abdomen, leading to the rectum. Pick it for the part of the colon just before the rectum.
The transverse colon crosses the upper abdomen from right to left. It would fit a question about the part of the colon held by the transverse mesocolon.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which part of the digestive tract is a narrow, worm-shaped, dead-end tube whose wall is rich in lymphatic tissue?
options: The cecum
The ileum
The sigmoid colon
The vermiform appendix
questions.why: Vermiform means worm-shaped, which describes the appendix well. It is a narrow, dead-end tube that hangs from the cecum at the start of the large intestine, and its wall is packed with lymphatic follicles. It belongs to the large intestine, not to the accessory digestive organs.
notes: The cecum is the wide pouch at the start of the large intestine that the appendix hangs from. Pick it for the structure just below the ileocecal valve.
The ileum is the long, final part of the small intestine, and its wall does carry lymphatic Peyer patches. It is not a narrow dead end, so pick it for the segment that joins the cecum.
The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped last part of the colon, leading to the rectum. It would be the answer for the part of the colon in the lower left abdomen.
Correct. The vermiform appendix is the worm-shaped lymphatic tube off the cecum.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A peptic ulcer begins in the mucosa of the stomach and erodes outward until it perforates the serosa. What is the main danger at that point?
options: Bile backs up into the gallbladder and liver
Stomach contents back up into the lower esophagus
Lumen contents spill into the peritoneal cavity
Lumen contents spill into the pleural cavity
questions.why: A peptic ulcer is an eroded sore in the wall of the stomach or duodenum. It starts in the mucosa and can work outward through the submucosa and muscularis. The serosa is the visceral peritoneum, so once the ulcer breaks through it, food, acid and bacteria leak into the peritoneal cavity, which can cause a serious infection of the peritoneum.
notes: Bile backing up toward the gallbladder and liver happens when a gallstone blocks the bile ducts. That would be the answer for a blocked common bile duct, not a perforated stomach.
Stomach contents moving up into the esophagus is reflux, caused by a weak lower esophageal sphincter rather than a hole in the wall. Choose it for a question about GERD or heartburn.
Correct. Breaking through the serosa opens the stomach into the peritoneal cavity.

The pleural cavity surrounds the lungs and lies above the diaphragm, so a hole in the stomach does not open into it. Students pick this when they mix up the serous membrane of the lungs with the peritoneum of the abdomen.
questions.answerText: Lumen contents spill into the peritoneal cavity

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The pyloric sphincter is a thickened ring at the outlet of the stomach. Which tissue forms it?
options: Smooth muscle
Dense regular connective tissue
Skeletal muscle
Hyaline cartilage
questions.why: The pyloric sphincter is a thickened ring of the circular smooth muscle in the stomach wall, located between the pylorus and the duodenum. Because it is smooth muscle, it works involuntarily, tightening and relaxing to control how fast stomach contents move into the small intestine. You cannot open or close it by choice.
notes: Correct. The pyloric sphincter is a ring of smooth muscle.

Dense regular connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments, which have parallel collagen fibers and no ability to contract. It would be the answer for a structure that resists pulling, not one that squeezes shut.
Skeletal muscle is the voluntary tissue that forms sphincters you can control, such as the external anal sphincter. Pick it for a question about a sphincter under conscious control.

Hyaline cartilage forms the C-shaped rings of the trachea and covers the ends of bones in joints. It holds a passage open rather than closing it, so it fits a question about the trachea, not a sphincter.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: How does the muscularis of the stomach differ from the muscularis of the rest of the canal?
options: It is made of skeletal rather than smooth muscle
It has only a single circular layer of smooth muscle
It adds a third, inner oblique muscle layer
It has a fibrous adventitia in place of a serosa
questions.why: Most of the canal has two layers of smooth muscle in its muscularis, an inner circular and an outer longitudinal layer. The stomach has three: an inner oblique layer, a middle circular layer, and an outer longitudinal layer. The extra oblique layer lets the stomach twist and churn its contents instead of only squeezing them forward.
notes: The stomach wall is smooth muscle like the rest of the tube, and it works without conscious control. Skeletal muscle in the digestive tract is found at the two ends, such as the external anal sphincter.
The stomach has more muscle layers than the rest of the tube, not fewer. Students pick this when they remember that the stomach is different but forget which way the difference goes.
Correct. The stomach adds an inner oblique layer, giving it three layers instead of two.
A fibrous adventitia replaces the serosa on the esophagus, not on the stomach. Pick this if the question asks how the outer layer of the esophagus differs from the rest of the canal.
questions.answerText: It adds a third, inner oblique muscle layer

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The stomach must churn food into a liquid, not just push it along. Which structural feature best supports this churning?
options: Villi that cover its mucosa
Gastric pits that lead to gastric glands
An inner oblique layer in its muscularis
Rugae that flatten as it fills
questions.why: Two layers of muscle can squeeze a tube narrower and shorter, which pushes contents forward. The stomach's third, inner oblique layer runs at an angle to the other two, so contracting all three together twists and kneads the contents. This churning mixes food with gastric juice until it becomes a liquid.
notes: Villi are finger-like projections of the mucosa in the small intestine, not the stomach. They increase surface area for absorption, which is the answer for a question about the small intestine lining.
Gastric pits lead down to the gastric glands, which secrete gastric juice. They are the answer for where the stomach's secretions come from, not for how it moves.
Correct. The extra oblique muscle layer lets the stomach churn as well as squeeze.
Rugae are folds of the stomach lining that flatten out as the stomach fills. They let the stomach expand to hold a meal, so they are the answer for a question about storage capacity, not mixing.
questions.answerText: An inner oblique layer in its muscularis

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence lists the three regions of the small intestine in the order food passes through them?
options: Duodenum, ileum, jejunum
Duodenum, jejunum, ileum
Ileum, jejunum, duodenum
Jejunum, duodenum, ileum
questions.why: Food leaves the stomach through the pyloric sphincter and enters the duodenum, the first and shortest region, about 25 cm (10 inches) long. It then moves through the jejunum, the middle region of about 1 m (3 feet), and finally the ileum, the longest region at about 2 m (6 feet). The ileum ends at the ileocecal sphincter, where it joins the large intestine.
notes: This swaps the last two regions. The ileum is the final region and the one that joins the large intestine, so it must come after the jejunum.
Correct. Food passes through the duodenum, then the jejunum, then the ileum.
This is the right sequence read backward, from the large intestine toward the stomach. Choose it only if a question asks you to trace the small intestine in reverse.
The jejunum is the middle region, so it cannot come first. The duodenum receives food directly from the stomach and must lead the sequence.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: What are the circular folds (plicae circulares) of the small intestine?
options: Folds of stomach lining that flatten when full
Microscopic projections on absorptive cells
Permanent ridges of the mucosa and submucosa
Finger-like projections of the mucosa alone
questions.why: Circular folds are permanent ridges that run around the inside of the small intestine. They are folds of both the mucosa and the submucosa, so unlike the rugae of the stomach, they do not flatten when the intestine fills. They are the largest of the three levels of folding that expand the absorptive surface, and villi cover their surface.
notes: Folds of the stomach lining that flatten as the stomach fills are rugae. Pick rugae for a question about how the stomach expands to hold a meal.

Microscopic projections on the surface of single absorptive cells are microvilli, which form the brush border. They are the smallest level of folding and the answer for a question about the brush border.
Correct. Circular folds are permanent ridges of both the mucosa and the submucosa.

Finger-like projections of the mucosa alone are villi, the middle level of folding that sits on top of the circular folds. They are the answer for the structures that give the lining its velvety look.
questions.answerText: Permanent ridges of the mucosa and submucosa

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: What is a lacteal?
options: A nerve network in the submucosa that controls secretion
A blood capillary in a villus that carries off sugars
A pouch of the colon wall formed by the teniae coli
A lymphatic capillary in a villus that absorbs fats
questions.why: Each villus of the small intestine has a core of lamina propria that holds a network of blood capillaries and one central lymphatic capillary, the lacteal. Digested fats are packaged into particles too large to enter the blood capillaries, so they enter the lacteal instead and travel in the lymph. The milky look of this fat-rich lymph gives the lacteal its name.
notes: A nerve network in the submucosa that controls secretions is the submucosal plexus. Choose it for a question about the enteric nervous system, not about absorbing fats.
Blood capillaries in the villus do absorb sugars and amino acids, but they are a separate network around the lacteal. Pick them if a question asks where most absorbed nutrients other than fats enter.
A pouch of the colon wall formed by the teniae coli is a haustrum. It would be the answer for the puckered pouches of the large intestine.
Correct. A lacteal is the lymphatic capillary in a villus that takes up dietary fats.
questions.answerText: A lymphatic capillary in a villus that absorbs fats

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The lining of the small intestine is folded at three scales to expand its surface for absorption. Which sequence lists them from largest to smallest?
options: Circular folds, villi, microvilli
Rugae, villi, microvilli
Microvilli, villi, circular folds
Villi, circular folds, microvilli
questions.why: The small intestine amplifies its surface three times over. Circular folds are ridges of the whole wall lining (mucosa and submucosa), villi are finger-like projections of the mucosa that cover those folds, and microvilli are microscopic projections on each absorptive cell that cover the villi. Each level sits on top of the one before it, which multiplies the area available for absorption.
notes: Correct. Circular folds are largest, villi cover them, and microvilli on single cells are smallest.
Rugae are folds of the stomach lining, not the small intestine, and they flatten when the stomach fills. The missing largest level of the small intestine is the circular folds.
This is the correct set read from smallest to largest. Choose it only if a question asks you to start with the microscopic level.
This puts villi ahead of circular folds, but villi are smaller and sit on top of the circular folds. Students pick this because villi are the best known of the three.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence lists the four parts of the colon in the order feces pass through them?
options: Ascending, descending, transverse, sigmoid
Ascending, transverse, descending, sigmoid
Sigmoid, descending, transverse, ascending
Transverse, ascending, descending, sigmoid
questions.why: The colon begins at the cecum in the lower right abdomen. The ascending colon rises along the right side, the transverse colon crosses the upper abdomen, the descending colon runs down the left side, and the S-shaped sigmoid colon curves toward the midline to join the rectum. Following that frame around the abdomen gives the order.
notes: This swaps the transverse and descending colon. The colon has to cross the abdomen before it can come down the left side, so the transverse colon comes second.
Correct. Ascending, transverse, descending, then sigmoid.
This is the correct sequence written backward, starting at the rectum. Pick it only if a question asks you to trace the colon in reverse.
The transverse colon cannot come first because the colon starts at the cecum in the lower right and must rise before it crosses. The ascending colon is the first part.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: What is the cecum?
options: The S-shaped final curve of the colon in the pelvis
The last few centimeters ending at the anus
The straight part lying in front of the sacrum
The pouch at the start of the large intestine
questions.why: The cecum is the blind-ended pouch where the large intestine begins, in the lower right abdomen just below the ileocecal valve. The ileum empties into it, and the narrow, worm-like vermiform appendix hangs from it. From the cecum, the large intestine continues upward as the ascending colon.
notes: The S-shaped final curve of the colon is the sigmoid colon, which joins the rectum. It is the answer for the last part of the colon on the left side of the pelvis.
The last few centimeters of the tract, ending at the anus, is the anal canal, not the cecum. Choose it for a question about where the internal and external anal sphincters sit.
The straight portion of the large intestine in front of the sacrum and coccyx is the rectum, not the cecum. Pick it for a question about the part that stores feces just before the anal canal.
Correct. The cecum is the first part of the large intestine, a pouch with the appendix attached.
questions.answerText: The pouch at the start of the large intestine

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: The haustra are the pouches that give the colon its puckered look. What forms them?
options: The omental appendices
The circular folds
The rugae
The teniae coli
questions.why: The teniae coli are three thickened bands of longitudinal muscle that run the length of the colon. They are shorter than the colon wall they attach to, so their steady tone gathers the wall into a row of pouches, the haustra. That is why the colon looks puckered rather than smooth.
notes: The omental appendices are small fat-filled pouches of peritoneum that hang from the colon surface, mostly along the teniae coli. They sit on the outside of the colon but do not form the haustra, so they are the answer for those fatty tags.
Circular folds are permanent ridges of the small intestine lining, not the colon. They are the answer for the largest level of folding in the small intestine.
Rugae are folds in the stomach lining that flatten as the stomach fills. Students pick them because they also give a wall a wrinkled look, but they belong to the stomach.
Correct. The teniae coli gather the colon wall into haustra.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which job belongs to the large intestine rather than the small intestine?
options: Absorbing leftover water and forming the feces
Churning food with acid into a liquid
Taking up dietary fats into lacteals
Absorbing most nutrients across the villi and microvilli
questions.why: By the time material reaches the large intestine, most nutrients have already been absorbed in the small intestine. The large intestine absorbs much of the water that is left and compacts the remaining material into feces, which it stores until elimination. It has no villi, which fits a job that is about water and waste rather than nutrient absorption.
notes: Correct. The large intestine absorbs the remaining water and forms and stores feces.
Churning food with acid until it becomes a liquid is the job of the stomach, with its three muscle layers and gastric glands. Choose it for a question about the stomach.
Lacteals are the lymphatic capillaries inside the villi of the small intestine. They are the answer for where dietary fats are absorbed, which is a small intestine job.
Absorbing most nutrients across villi is the job of the small intestine, whose circular folds, villi and microvilli give it a huge surface. Pick it for a question about where most absorption happens.
questions.answerText: Absorbing leftover water and forming the feces

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: What does the pyloric sphincter separate?
options: The ileum from the cecum
The pylorus of the stomach from the duodenum
The esophagus from the cardia of the stomach
The duodenum from the jejunum
questions.why: The pyloric sphincter is a ring of smooth muscle at the outlet of the stomach. It sits between the pylorus, the last part of the stomach, and the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. By tightening and relaxing it controls how quickly stomach contents pass into the small intestine.
notes: The junction between the ileum and the cecum is guarded by the ileocecal sphincter. That is the answer for the passage from the small to the large intestine.
Correct. The pyloric sphincter lies between the pylorus and the duodenum.
The junction of the esophagus and the cardia is guarded by the lower esophageal sphincter. Pick it for the sphincter at the entrance of the stomach.
The duodenum continues into the jejunum without a named sphincter. Students pick this because both are parts of the small intestine near the stomach, but no sphincter separates them.
questions.answerText: The pylorus of the stomach from the duodenum

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: What does the ileocecal sphincter separate?
options: The sigmoid colon from the rectum
The ileum from the cecum
The jejunum from the ileum
The stomach from the duodenum
questions.why: The ileocecal sphincter is a thickening of smooth muscle where the ileum, the last part of the small intestine, empties into the cecum, the first part of the large intestine. Together with folds of mucosa it forms the ileocecal valve, which keeps the contents of the large intestine from moving back into the ileum. It sits in the lower right abdomen.
notes: The sigmoid colon joins the rectum without a named sphincter. The sphincters at the end of the tract are the internal and external anal sphincters, which guard the anus.
Correct. The ileocecal sphincter lies between the ileum and the cecum.
The jejunum blends into the ileum without a sphincter, and both lie within the small intestine. Students pick this when they remember the ileum is involved but forget which neighbor it meets.
The stomach and duodenum are separated by the pyloric sphincter. That is the answer for the outlet of the stomach.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which sequence traces food from the mouth to the anus through the named regions of the canal?
options: Mouth, pharynx, stomach, esophagus, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, esophagus, pharynx, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, large intestine, small intestine
questions.why: Food moves through the alimentary canal in one direction. It is chewed in the mouth, swallowed through the pharynx, carried down the esophagus, churned in the stomach, absorbed mainly in the small intestine, and turned into feces in the large intestine before leaving through the anus. Each region hands its contents to the next.
notes: This swaps the stomach and esophagus. The esophagus is the tube that carries food down to the stomach, so it has to come first.
Correct. The pathway runs mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, then anus.
This puts the esophagus ahead of the pharynx, but food must pass through the pharynx at the back of the throat before it can enter the esophagus.
This swaps the two intestines. The small intestine receives food directly from the stomach, and the large intestine comes last, which is easy to forget because the names describe width, not order.
questions.answerText: Mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Which statement correctly matches the main jobs of the small and large intestines?
options: Small: most nutrient absorption; large: absorbs leftover water, forms feces
Small: stores the feces; large: absorbs fats into the lacteals
Small: churns food into a liquid; large: most nutrient absorption
Small: absorbs leftover water, forms feces; large: most nutrient absorption
questions.why: The small intestine, with its circular folds, villi and microvilli, has an enormous surface and is where most absorption occurs. By the time material reaches the large intestine, most nutrients are gone, so the large intestine absorbs much of the water that remains and forms and stores the feces. The large intestine has no villi, which fits a job about water and waste rather than nutrient absorption.
notes: Correct. Most absorption is in the small intestine, and the large intestine reclaims leftover water and forms feces.
Lacteals are in the villi of the small intestine, and feces are stored in the large intestine. This pairing puts both jobs in the wrong organ.
Churning food into a liquid is the job of the stomach, not the small intestine. Pick churning for a question about the stomach and its three muscle layers.

This swaps the two intestines. Most nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine, whose circular folds and villi give it a huge surface, while the large intestine has no villi and mainly reclaims water and forms feces.
questions.answerText: Small: most nutrient absorption; large: absorbs leftover water, forms feces

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: Appendicitis is inflammation of the vermiform appendix. Why is a ruptured appendix especially dangerous?
options: It pushes part of the stomach up through the diaphragm
It can block the flow of bile into the duodenum
It lets stomach acid back up into the esophagus
It can spread infection into the peritoneal cavity
questions.why: The vermiform appendix is a narrow, worm-like tube of lymphatic tissue attached to the cecum. When it is inflamed it can swell and burst, releasing bacteria-laden contents into the peritoneal cavity. Infection can then spread across the peritoneum, the large serous membrane lining the abdomen, which is why appendicitis is treated as an emergency.
notes: Part of the stomach pushing up through the diaphragm is a hiatal hernia. That is the answer for a question about the esophageal hiatus, not the appendix.
Blocking the flow of bile into the duodenum is caused by a gallstone in the bile ducts. Pick it for a question about gallstones or jaundice.
Stomach acid backing up into the esophagus is reflux through a weak lower esophageal sphincter, as in GERD. It is the answer for heartburn behind the sternum.
Correct. A ruptured appendix can spread infection through the peritoneal cavity.
questions.answerText: It can spread infection into the peritoneal cavity

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A patient has pain that settles in the lower right abdomen. Which structure of the canal is classically involved?
options: Sigmoid colon
Gallbladder
Appendix
Stomach
questions.why: Where a problem sits in the abdomen predicts where the patient feels it. The vermiform appendix hangs from the cecum, which lies in the lower right abdomen, so pain that settles there classically points to appendicitis. This is one reason anatomists divide the abdomen into quadrants and regions.
notes: The sigmoid colon curves through the lower left abdomen into the pelvis. Pick it for lower left pain, such as inflammation of pouches in the colon wall.
The gallbladder sits under the liver in the upper right abdomen. It would be the answer for upper right pain after a fatty meal, as with gallstones.
Correct. The appendix lies in the lower right abdomen, so pain there suggests appendicitis.
The stomach lies in the upper abdomen, mostly to the left of the midline below the diaphragm. It is the answer for upper abdominal pain, as with a peptic ulcer.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A swallowed camera pill travels from the pylorus to the anus. Which is the first sphincter made of skeletal muscle that it passes?
options: The external anal sphincter.
The ileocecal sphincter.
The pyloric sphincter.
The internal anal sphincter.
questions.why: Only the two ends of the canal have skeletal muscle sphincters: the upper esophageal sphincter at the top and the external anal sphincter at the bottom. Starting at the pylorus, the pill passes the pyloric sphincter, the ileocecal sphincter, and the internal anal sphincter, all smooth muscle. The external anal sphincter, outside the internal one, is the first skeletal muscle sphincter it meets, which is why it is the one under voluntary control.
notes: Correct. Every sphincter from the pylorus onward is smooth muscle until the external anal sphincter at the very end.
The ileocecal sphincter is a thickening of smooth muscle at the end of the ileum, where it opens into the cecum.
The pyloric sphincter is a thick ring of circular smooth muscle around the pylorus, between the stomach and the duodenum.
The internal anal sphincter is a thickening of the circular smooth muscle of the anal canal, so it is involuntary smooth muscle.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A swallowed coin stops in the esophagus inside the thorax, above the diaphragm. Which sphincter did it most recently pass through, and what tissue forms that sphincter?
options: The upper esophageal sphincter, made of smooth muscle.
The pyloric sphincter, made of smooth muscle.
The lower esophageal sphincter, made of smooth muscle.
The upper esophageal sphincter, made of skeletal muscle.
questions.why: The upper esophageal sphincter sits at the top of the esophagus, at the level of the cricoid cartilage, and separates the laryngopharynx from the esophagus. It is skeletal muscle, continuous with the muscles of the pharynx. The next sphincter, the lower esophageal sphincter, is at the bottom of the esophagus below the diaphragm. A coin stuck in the thoracic esophagus has passed only the upper one.
notes: The sphincter is right, but it is skeletal muscle. Only the two ends of the canal have skeletal muscle sphincters, and this is the top one.
The pyloric sphincter is at the outlet of the stomach. A coin still in the esophagus is far above it.
The lower esophageal sphincter is at the bottom of the esophagus, just below the diaphragm. A coin stuck above the diaphragm has not reached it.
Correct. The coin entered the esophagus through the upper esophageal sphincter, which is skeletal muscle continuous with the pharynx.
questions.answerText: The upper esophageal sphincter, made of skeletal muscle.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A camera pill shows a thickened ring of smooth muscle with folds of mucosa, forming a valve. On the far side is a blind pouch. Which sphincter is this, and which two regions does it separate?
options: The internal anal sphincter, between the anal canal and the outside.
The lower esophageal sphincter, between the esophagus and stomach.
The ileocecal sphincter, between the ileum and the cecum.
The pyloric sphincter, between the stomach and the duodenum.
questions.why: Two clues identify it. The ileocecal sphincter is a thickening of smooth muscle at the end of the ileum that, together with folds of mucosa, forms the ileocecal valve. The cecum, the first part of the large intestine, is a blind pouch below that valve. So this sphincter separates the small intestine (ileum) from the large intestine (cecum).
notes: The internal anal sphincter opens to the outside of the body at the anus, so nothing lies beyond it inside the canal.
The lower esophageal sphincter opens into the cardia of the stomach. The stomach is a J-shaped widening of the tube, not a blind pouch.
Correct. The ileocecal sphincter and mucosal folds form the ileocecal valve, and the blind pouch beyond it is the cecum.
The pyloric sphincter is a ring of circular smooth muscle at the pylorus. The duodenum beyond it is a C-shaped tube, not a blind pouch.
questions.answerText: The ileocecal sphincter, between the ileum and the cecum.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: An ulcer sits on the short, concave border of the stomach, on the right side facing the liver. Which border is this, and which peritoneal fold attaches along it?
options: The lesser curvature, where the lesser omentum attaches.
The greater curvature, where the lesser omentum attaches.
The greater curvature, where the greater omentum hangs.
The lesser curvature, where the greater omentum hangs.
questions.why: The stomach has two borders. The lesser curvature is the short, concave border on the right (medial) side, facing the liver, and the lesser omentum runs from it up to the liver. The greater curvature is the long, convex border on the left (lateral) side, and the greater omentum hangs from it. Matching the size words, lesser goes with lesser and greater goes with greater.
notes: Correct. The short, concave right border is the lesser curvature, and the lesser omentum attaches along it.
This mixes the two. The lesser omentum runs from the lesser curvature to the liver, and the greater curvature is the long, convex border.
The greater curvature is the long, convex left border, and the greater omentum hangs from it. The ulcer is on the short, concave border.
The border is right, but the greater omentum hangs from the greater curvature. The lesser omentum attaches to the lesser curvature.
questions.answerText: The lesser curvature, where the lesser omentum attaches.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: On the cadaver, you follow the three teniae coli down the ascending colon to the point where they meet. What do you find there, and which part of the large intestine is it attached to?
options: The ileocecal valve, on the cecum.
The hepatic flexure, under the liver.
The base of the appendix, on the rectum.
The base of the appendix, on the cecum.
questions.why: The teniae coli are three flat ribbons of smooth muscle along the cecum and colon. Following them down the ascending colon leads to the cecum, the blind pouch at the start of the large intestine. The three teniae meet at the base of the vermiform appendix, which is one way to find the appendix on a specimen.
notes: The ileocecal valve is where the ileum opens into the large intestine. The teniae coli meet at the base of the appendix, not at the valve.
The hepatic flexure is the bend at the top of the ascending colon. Following the teniae down the ascending colon leads away from it, to the cecum.
The landmark is right, but the appendix is attached to the cecum. The teniae spread out into a full layer at the rectum, which is in the pelvis.
Correct. The three teniae meet at the base of the vermiform appendix, which hangs from the cecum.
questions.answerText: The base of the appendix, on the cecum.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: As material moves through the colon, which bend does it pass between the transverse colon and the descending colon?
options: The splenic (left colic) flexure.
The hepatic (right colic) flexure.
The sigmoid colon.
The ileocecal valve.
questions.why: The colon frames the small intestine. Material rises in the ascending colon, turns at the hepatic flexure under the liver, crosses the abdomen in the transverse colon from right to left, then turns down at the splenic flexure near the spleen into the descending colon. The two flexures are bends between the parts of the colon, not separate parts.
notes: Correct. The transverse colon crosses the abdomen from right to left and turns down at the splenic flexure, the bend near the spleen, into the descending colon.
The hepatic flexure is the bend under the liver between the ascending and transverse colon. Material passes it before the transverse colon, not after.
The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped curve into the pelvis. It comes after the descending colon, so material reaches it later.
The ileocecal valve sits between the ileum and the cecum, at the start of the large intestine, well before the transverse colon.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A swallowed seed is found in the transverse colon. In order, which named structures did it pass after leaving the ileum?
options: Pyloric sphincter, cecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure.
Ileocecal valve, appendix, ascending colon, hepatic flexure.
Ileocecal valve, cecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure.
Ileocecal valve, cecum, descending colon, splenic flexure.
questions.why: The colon frames the small intestine. Leaving the ileum, material passes the ileocecal sphincter (ileocecal valve) into the cecum, then travels up the right side in the ascending colon. The bend under the liver, the hepatic flexure, turns it left into the transverse colon. The appendix is off the main path, and the splenic flexure and descending colon come later.
notes: The pyloric sphincter sits between the stomach and the duodenum. The sphincter at the end of the ileum is the ileocecal sphincter, which forms the ileocecal valve.
The appendix is a blind tube hanging from the cecum, so food never travels through it. The seed passes through the cecum instead.
Correct. From the ileum, material crosses the ileocecal valve into the cecum, rises in the ascending colon, and turns at the hepatic flexure into the transverse colon.
The descending colon and splenic flexure come after the transverse colon, on the left side. The seed reached the transverse colon from the right side.
questions.answerText: Ileocecal valve, cecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure.

questions.topic: Stomach, small intestine and large intestine
questions.q: A bolus is in the laryngopharynx. Which structure covers the larynx so the bolus does not enter it, and which named structure does the bolus pass through next?
options: The epiglottis; next, the upper esophageal sphincter.
The epiglottis; next, the lower esophageal sphincter.
The uvula; next, the fauces into the oropharynx.
The soft palate; next, the upper esophageal sphincter.
questions.why: In the laryngopharynx the air and food paths split. The epiglottis covers the larynx, so the bolus passes behind it toward the esophagus. The upper esophageal sphincter, at the level of the cricoid cartilage, then relaxes to let the bolus into the esophagus. The soft palate and uvula worked earlier, closing off the nasopharynx while the bolus was in the oropharynx.
notes: Correct. The epiglottis covers the larynx, and the bolus passes behind it and through the upper esophageal sphincter into the esophagus.
The epiglottis is right, but the lower esophageal sphincter is at the bottom of the esophagus. The bolus meets the upper one first.
The uvula helps close the nasopharynx, and the fauces lead from the mouth into the oropharynx. A bolus in the laryngopharynx has already passed both.
The soft palate and uvula close off the nasopharynx, higher up. They do not cover the larynx.
questions.answerText: The epiglottis; next, the upper esophageal sphincter.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas are grouped together as what?
options: The accessory digestive organs
Lymphatic organs of the gut
Retroperitoneal organs
Organs of the alimentary canal
questions.why: The digestive system has two groups of organs. The alimentary canal is the tube that food passes through, while the accessory digestive organs sit alongside it and help digestion without being part of the tube. The teeth and tongue work on food in the mouth, and the salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas empty their secretions into the canal.
notes: Correct. These six help digestion from outside the food tube, which is what makes them the accessory digestive organs.
Lymphatic tissue of the gut, such as the tonsils and the appendix, holds immune cells. None of the six organs listed is lymphatic tissue, so this group does not fit.
Retroperitoneal organs lie behind the peritoneum, such as the kidneys, pancreas, and duodenum. The pancreas fits, but the liver, gallbladder, and tongue do not, so this group does not match the list.
The alimentary canal is the tube food passes through, from the mouth to the anus. None of these six organs is part of that tube, so this group is the opposite of the right answer.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which list correctly matches each of the three large pairs of salivary glands to its location?
options: Parotid along the inner mandible, submandibular beneath the tongue, sublingual in front of and below the ear
Parotid beneath the tongue, submandibular in front of and below the ear, sublingual along the inner mandible
Parotid in front of and below the ear, submandibular beneath the tongue, sublingual along the inner mandible
Parotid in front of and below the ear, submandibular along the inner mandible, sublingual beneath the tongue
questions.why: The parotid glands sit anterior and inferior to each ear, between the skin and the masseter muscle. The submandibular glands lie in the floor of the mouth along the inner side of the mandible, and the sublingual glands sit beneath the tongue, just above the submandibular glands. The names help: sub-mandibular means under the jaw, and sub-lingual means under the tongue.
notes: This list puts every gland in the wrong spot. The parotid sits by the ear, the gland along the inner mandible is the submandibular, and the sublingual sits under the tongue.
This list moves every gland to the wrong spot. The parotid is the gland by the ear, not under the tongue, so use the name parotid (para means beside, otic means ear) to anchor it next to the ear.
The parotid is placed correctly, but the other two are swapped. The submandibular lies along the inner mandible, and the sublingual lies beneath the tongue, just above the submandibular.
Correct. Each name gives the spot: parotid means beside the ear, submandibular means below the mandible, and sublingual means below the tongue.
questions.answerText: Parotid in front of and below the ear, submandibular along the inner mandible, sublingual beneath the tongue

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which list names the four lobes of the liver?
options: Head, body, tail, and caudate
Right, left, superior, and inferior
Superior, middle, inferior, and quadrate
Right, left, quadrate, and caudate
questions.why: The liver has two large principal lobes, the right and left, separated on the anterior surface by the falciform ligament. On the posterior and inferior surface you can also see two small lobes, the quadrate lobe and the caudate lobe. All four are on the lab structure list, so practice finding the two small lobes when the liver is turned over.
notes: Head, body, and tail are the three regions of the pancreas. That set would be right for a question about pancreas regions, not liver lobes.
Superior and inferior are lobe names for the lungs, not the liver. The left lung has a superior and an inferior lobe, so this list mixes liver lobes with lung lobes.
Superior, middle, and inferior are the three lobes of the right lung. Pick that set if the question asked about the right lung; only the quadrate lobe here belongs to the liver.
Correct. The right and left lobes are seen from the front, and the quadrate and caudate lobes are the two small lobes seen from below and behind.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which group of structures passes through the porta hepatis on the underside of the liver?
options: The hepatic portal vein, inferior vena cava, and pancreatic duct
