The hepatic veins, hepatic portal vein, and common bile duct
The hepatic portal vein, hepatic artery, and hepatic ducts
The hepatic veins, hepatic artery, and cystic duct
questions.why: The porta hepatis is the gateway on the inferior surface of the liver. Two vessels bring blood in through it, the hepatic portal vein (nutrient-rich blood from the digestive organs) and the hepatic artery (oxygen-rich blood), while the right and left hepatic ducts carry bile out. The common bile duct does not pass through it, because that duct forms below the liver where the common hepatic duct meets the cystic duct.
notes: The inferior vena cava runs along the back of the liver, not through the porta hepatis, and the pancreatic duct never reaches the liver. The vena cava would be the answer for the vessel that receives the hepatic veins.

This mixes in two structures that do not belong. The hepatic veins leave from the back of the liver, and the common bile duct forms outside the liver, below the porta hepatis, where the common hepatic and cystic ducts join.
Correct. The hepatic portal vein and hepatic artery bring blood in at the porta hepatis, and the right and left hepatic ducts carry bile out.

The hepatic veins drain blood out of the liver into the inferior vena cava from the back of the liver, not through the porta hepatis, and the cystic duct belongs to the gallbladder. Pick the hepatic veins for a question about where blood leaves the liver.
questions.answerText: The hepatic portal vein, hepatic artery, and hepatic ducts

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the hepatic sinusoids and the bile canaliculi?
options: Both carry blood, but sinusoids carry arterial blood and canaliculi carry portal blood
Sinusoids carry blood between the plates of hepatocytes, and canaliculi collect bile between the hepatocytes
Both carry bile, but sinusoids drain to the gallbladder and canaliculi drain to the duodenum
Sinusoids collect bile between the hepatocytes, and canaliculi carry blood between the plates of hepatocytes
questions.why: Hepatocytes, the liver's working cells, are stacked in thin plates called hepatic laminae. The hepatic sinusoids are wide, leaky capillaries that run between the plates, so blood flows right past the cells. The bile canaliculi are tiny channels between neighboring hepatocytes that collect the bile those cells make, so blood and bile travel in separate channels.
notes: Only the sinusoids carry blood; they receive a mix of arterial and portal blood. The canaliculi never carry blood, since their job is to collect bile from the hepatocytes.
Correct. Sinusoids are leaky capillaries that carry blood past the plates, while canaliculi are tiny bile channels between neighboring hepatocytes.
Only the canaliculi carry bile. Sinusoids are blood capillaries, and bile reaches the gallbladder and duodenum through the duct system, not directly from either channel.
This swaps the two jobs. Sinusoids are capillaries carrying blood and canaliculi carry bile, so remember that canaliculi (little canals) are the bile channels.
questions.answerText: Sinusoids carry blood between the plates of hepatocytes, and canaliculi collect bile between the hepatocytes

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Bile made by hepatocytes leaves the liver through a series of widening channels. Which sequence is correct, starting at the hepatocytes?
options: Hepatic sinusoids, right and left hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct
Bile canaliculi, right and left hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct
Right and left hepatic ducts, bile canaliculi, common bile duct
Bile canaliculi, common hepatic duct, right and left hepatic ducts
questions.why: Bile drains from small channels into larger ones, like streams joining a river. The tiny bile canaliculi between hepatocytes collect it first, then the bile is gathered into the right and left hepatic ducts, and those two merge into the single common hepatic duct as they leave the liver. From there bile can detour up the cystic duct to the gallbladder or continue in the common bile duct.
notes: Hepatic sinusoids are blood capillaries between the hepatocyte plates, not bile channels. Pick the sinusoids if the question asked where blood flows past the hepatocytes.
Correct. Bile starts in the canaliculi, gathers into the right and left hepatic ducts, and those merge into the common hepatic duct.

The canaliculi are the very first channels, right between the hepatocytes, so they cannot come after the hepatic ducts. The common bile duct also forms later, below the liver, once the cystic duct joins.
This reverses the last two steps. The right and left hepatic ducts come first and merge into the common hepatic duct, so one common duct cannot split back into two on the way out.
questions.answerText: Bile canaliculi, right and left hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which region of the gallbladder is the broad, rounded end at its inferior tip?
options: The fundus
The cardia
The body
The neck
questions.why: The gallbladder has three regions: the fundus, the body, and the neck. The fundus is the broad, rounded inferior end, the body is the middle, and the neck tapers at the superior end where the sac narrows into the cystic duct. The stomach also has a region called the fundus, so the word simply means the rounded end or base of a hollow organ.
notes: Correct. The fundus is the wide, rounded end that sticks out past the lower edge of the liver.
The cardia is the region of the stomach that surrounds the opening from the esophagus. It is not part of the gallbladder, though the stomach does share the term fundus with it.
The body is the middle portion of the gallbladder, between the fundus and the neck. Pick it for the central part of the sac, not the rounded tip.
The neck is the tapered superior end of the gallbladder that leads into the cystic duct. It would be the answer if the question asked which region connects to the cystic duct.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which pancreatic duct empties separately into the duodenum instead of joining the common bile duct?
options: The cystic duct
The common hepatic duct
The accessory pancreatic duct
The main pancreatic duct
questions.why: The pancreas usually drains through two ducts. The main pancreatic duct, also called the duct of Wirsung, joins the common bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla. The smaller accessory duct, also called the duct of Santorini, drains part of the head and empties into the duodenum on its own at the minor duodenal papilla, so only the main duct shares an opening with bile.
notes: The cystic duct connects the gallbladder to the bile duct system and carries no pancreatic juice. It would be the answer for the duct that carries bile to and from the gallbladder.
The common hepatic duct is a bile duct, not a pancreatic duct. It carries bile out of the liver and joins the cystic duct to make the common bile duct.
Correct. The accessory duct (duct of Santorini) opens on its own at the minor duodenal papilla, a little above the major papilla.
The main pancreatic duct (duct of Wirsung) is the one that does join the common bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla. Pick it if the question asked which pancreatic duct meets the bile duct.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Pancreatic juice made by the acini drains through the pancreatic ducts. Where does it finally empty?
options: The stomach
The gallbladder
The bloodstream
The duodenum
questions.why: The acini are the exocrine clusters of the pancreas. Exocrine glands release their products through ducts onto a surface, and for the pancreas that surface is the lining of the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. The main pancreatic duct delivers juice through the hepatopancreatic ampulla, and the accessory duct empties separately, but both end in the duodenum.
notes: The stomach sits in front of the pancreas, but no pancreatic duct opens into it. The stomach would be the answer if the question asked where gastric juice is made.
The gallbladder stores bile from the liver and receives no pancreatic juice. Pick it if the question asked where bile is stored and concentrated between meals.
The bloodstream is where the endocrine pancreatic islets release their hormones, without ducts. It would be the answer for islet hormones, not for pancreatic juice from the acini.
Correct. Both pancreatic ducts end in the duodenum, so that is where pancreatic juice is delivered.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Starting at the common bile duct, which sequence shows the rest of bile's route into the small intestine?
options: Common bile duct, cystic duct, gallbladder, duodenum
Common bile duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, major duodenal papilla, duodenum
Common bile duct, pancreatic duct, pyloric sphincter, stomach
Common bile duct, major duodenal papilla, hepatopancreatic ampulla, duodenum
questions.why: The common bile duct runs down to meet the main pancreatic duct, and the two join in a short widened passage called the hepatopancreatic ampulla. The ampulla opens into the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla, a small raised bump on the duodenal lining, with the sphincter of Oddi controlling the flow. The papilla is the doorway, so it has to come last before the duodenum.
notes: The cystic duct and gallbladder lie upstream of the common bile duct, so this route runs backward. It would describe bile backing up into the gallbladder for storage, not bile heading into the intestine.
Correct. The common bile duct empties into the ampulla, and the ampulla opens into the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla.

Bile never flows into the stomach through a normal route, and the pyloric sphincter guards the exit from the stomach into the duodenum. Pick the pyloric sphincter for a question about stomach emptying.
The ampulla and the papilla are in the wrong order. Bile and pancreatic juice meet in the ampulla first and then pass out through the papilla, which is the opening on the duodenal wall.
questions.answerText: Common bile duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, major duodenal papilla, duodenum

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Hepatocytes are arranged in thin plates with blood channels running between them. What are these plates called?
options: Acini
Portal triads
Bile canaliculi
Hepatic laminae
questions.why: Hepatocytes, the functional cells of the liver, are lined up in plates called hepatic laminae (lamina means a thin sheet). Wide, leaky capillaries called hepatic sinusoids run between the plates, so nearly every hepatocyte has blood flowing right past it. This arrangement lets the cells pull nutrients from the blood and add products back to it.
notes: Acini are the exocrine clusters of the pancreas that make pancreatic juice. They would be the answer for the main tissue of the pancreas, not the liver.

A portal triad is the trio of a bile duct, a hepatic artery branch, and a hepatic portal vein branch at each corner of a liver lobule. Pick it if the question asked what sits at the corners of a lobule.
Bile canaliculi are tiny channels between hepatocytes that collect bile. Pick them if the question asked where bile first drains, not what the cell plates are called.
Correct. Lamina means a thin sheet, and the plates of hepatocytes are called the hepatic laminae.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which set correctly matches each large salivary gland to where its duct opens into the mouth?
options: Parotid beside the upper second molar, submandibular near the lingual frenulum, sublingual along the floor of the mouth
Parotid near the lingual frenulum, submandibular beside the upper second molar, sublingual along the floor of the mouth
Parotid along the floor of the mouth, submandibular near the lingual frenulum, sublingual beside the upper second molar
Parotid beside the lower incisors, submandibular beside the upper second molar, sublingual near the lingual frenulum
questions.why: Each duct opens close to its gland. The parotid gland sits by the ear, so its duct crosses the cheek and opens on the inside of the cheek beside the upper second molar. The submandibular ducts open near the lingual frenulum under the tongue, and the sublingual glands drain through several small ducts onto the floor of the mouth.
notes: Correct. The parotid duct crosses the cheek to the upper second molar, the submandibular duct opens beside the frenulum, and the sublingual ducts open along the floor of the mouth.
This swaps the parotid and submandibular openings. The parotid duct opens high in the cheek beside the upper second molar, while the submandibular ducts open low, near the lingual frenulum.
The parotid duct does not open on the floor of the mouth, and the sublingual ducts do not reach the upper molars. Only the submandibular opening is placed correctly here.
No large salivary duct opens beside the lower incisors in the cheek, and the submandibular duct opens under the tongue, not by the upper molar. This set scrambles all three.
questions.answerText: Parotid beside the upper second molar, submandibular near the lingual frenulum, sublingual along the floor of the mouth

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which of these structures is NOT one of the six accessory digestive organs?
options: The pancreas
The vermiform appendix
The gallbladder
The tongue
questions.why: The six accessory digestive organs are the teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas. The vermiform appendix is a small tube of lymphatic tissue attached to the cecum, so it is part of the large intestine, which belongs to the alimentary canal itself. Accessory organs help digestion from outside the food tube, while the appendix is a branch of the tube.
notes: The pancreas is one of the six accessory organs, since it sends pancreatic juice to the duodenum through its ducts. Because it belongs to the group, it cannot be the exception.
Correct. The appendix hangs from the cecum, so it is part of the large intestine, not one of the accessory organs.
The gallbladder is one of the six accessory organs. It stores and concentrates bile, so it belongs to the group and is not the exception.
The tongue is one of the six accessory organs. Along with the teeth it works on food in the mouth, so it belongs to the group and is not the exception.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which is the largest of the three large pairs of salivary glands?
options: The parotid glands
The submandibular glands
The sublingual glands
The buccal glands
questions.why: The parotid glands are the largest salivary glands. Each one sits anterior and inferior to the ear, between the skin and the masseter muscle, and its duct crosses the cheek to open beside the upper second molar. Their size and position are why swelling from mumps shows so clearly at the angle of the jaw.
notes: Correct. The parotids are the largest of the three pairs, bigger than both the submandibular and sublingual glands.
The submandibular glands are one of the three large pairs, but they are smaller than the parotids. They would be the answer for the glands that lie along the inner side of the mandible.
The sublingual glands are the smallest of the three large pairs and sit beneath the tongue. Pick them for the glands that drain through several small ducts onto the floor of the mouth.
The buccal glands are minor salivary glands scattered in the lining of the cheek, not one of the three large pairs. They would fit a question about the small glands of the mouth lining.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which structure stores and concentrates bile between meals?
options: The gallbladder
The liver
The duodenum
The pancreas
questions.why: The gallbladder is a pear-shaped sac on the posterior surface of the liver. Bile made in the liver backs up through the cystic duct into the gallbladder, where it is stored and concentrated until a meal arrives. It is the only accessory organ that works as a storage organ rather than as a gland.
notes: Correct. The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile.
The liver makes bile but does not store it. Pick the liver if the question asked which organ produces bile.
The duodenum is where bile is delivered, through the major duodenal papilla. Pick it for the part of the small intestine that receives bile and pancreatic juice.
The pancreas makes pancreatic juice and hormones, not bile. It would be the answer for the accessory organ that has both acini and islets.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which organ is the largest gland in the body?
options: The liver
The pancreas
The thyroid gland
The parotid gland
questions.why: The liver is the largest gland in the body. It sits just below the diaphragm, mostly in the right upper quadrant, and its main digestive job is producing bile. It counts as a gland because its cells make and release products, including bile into the ducts and plasma proteins into the blood.
notes: Correct. The liver is the largest gland in the body.
The pancreas is a large gland behind the stomach, but it is much smaller than the liver. Pick it if the question asked which gland is both exocrine and endocrine.
The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped endocrine gland in the neck, far smaller than the liver. It would be the answer for the gland that wraps the front of the trachea just below the larynx.
The parotid is the largest salivary gland, not the largest gland overall. Pick it for the salivary gland in front of and below the ear.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Where is the pancreas located?
options: On the posterior surface of the liver
Posterior to the stomach
In the lower right quadrant beside the cecum
Anterior to the stomach
questions.why: The pancreas is a soft, tapering gland that lies posterior to the stomach, against the posterior abdominal wall in a retroperitoneal position. Its head sits in the C-shaped curve of the duodenum and its tail reaches toward the spleen. Because it hides behind the stomach, you usually have to lift the stomach to see it on a model.
notes: The posterior surface of the liver is where the gallbladder sits. Pick that location for the gallbladder, not the pancreas.
Correct. The pancreas lies posterior to the stomach.
The lower right quadrant beside the cecum is where the appendix lies. That location would be the answer for the appendix, not a gland in the upper abdomen.
The pancreas is hidden behind the stomach, not in front of it. In front of the stomach is the anterior abdominal wall, with the left lobe of the liver reaching over the stomach higher up.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: What is the name of the main functional cell of the liver?
options: Goblet cells
Hepatocytes
Islet cells
Acinar cells
questions.why: Hepatocytes (hepat means liver, cyte means cell) are the functional cells of the liver. They are arranged in plates called hepatic laminae, they make bile, and they process the nutrients delivered by the blood flowing past them in the sinusoids. Almost every liver job you learn traces back to hepatocytes.
notes: Goblet cells are mucus-secreting cells scattered in the epithelium lining the intestines and airways. Pick them for a question about mucus production in a simple columnar epithelium.
Correct. Hepat means liver and cyte means cell, so hepatocytes are the working cells of the liver.
Islet cells form the pancreatic islets, the endocrine clusters of the pancreas. They would be the answer for the pancreatic cells that release hormones into the blood.
Acinar cells make up the acini, the exocrine clusters of the pancreas. Pick them for the cells that produce pancreatic juice.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Under the microscope, the liver is built of many small, roughly hexagonal units. What is each unit called?
options: A portal triad
A liver lobe
A hepatic sinusoid
A liver lobule
questions.why: A liver lobule is a small, roughly six-sided unit of plates of hepatocytes arranged around a central vein. At each corner of the lobule sits a portal triad. Thousands of lobules packed together make up each of the large lobes you see with the naked eye.
notes: A portal triad is the bile duct, hepatic artery branch, and hepatic portal vein branch found at each corner of a lobule. It is part of the lobule, so it would be the answer for what sits at the corners.
A lobe is a large division of the whole liver, such as the right or left lobe, visible without a microscope. Pick it for the big named parts of the liver, not the tiny units.
A hepatic sinusoid is one of the leaky capillaries running between plates of hepatocytes inside the lobule. Pick it for the blood channels within the lobule.
Correct. The liver lobule is the small six-sided unit, with a central vein in the middle and a portal triad at each corner.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which duct carries pancreatic juice from the pancreas and joins the common bile duct?
options: The common bile duct
The main pancreatic duct
The cystic duct
The common hepatic duct
questions.why: The main pancreatic duct, also called the duct of Wirsung, runs the length of the pancreas collecting pancreatic juice from the acini. Near the duodenum it joins the common bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla, and the combined fluid enters the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla. This shared ending is why a stone at the ampulla can affect the pancreas.
notes: The common bile duct is the duct that the pancreatic duct joins, but it carries bile, not pancreatic juice. It would be the answer for the duct formed by the common hepatic and cystic ducts.
Correct. The main pancreatic duct runs the length of the pancreas collecting juice and joins the common bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla.
The cystic duct carries bile to and from the gallbladder. It would be the answer for the duct that connects the gallbladder to the bile duct system.
The common hepatic duct carries bile out of the liver after the right and left hepatic ducts merge. Pick it for the duct that the cystic duct joins.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which fold of peritoneum attaches the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm?
options: The greater omentum
The falciform ligament
The lesser omentum
The mesentery
questions.why: The falciform ligament is a thin, sickle-shaped fold of peritoneum (falx means sickle) that suspends the liver from the anterior abdominal wall and the diaphragm. On the anterior surface it also marks the boundary between the right and left lobes. Its free lower edge carries the ligamentum teres, the remnant of the fetal umbilical vein.
notes: The greater omentum is the fatty apron that hangs from the stomach over the intestines. It does not attach the liver to the body wall, so pick it for the largest peritoneal fold.
Correct. The falciform ligament is the sickle-shaped fold that holds the liver to the diaphragm and the anterior abdominal wall.
The lesser omentum connects the liver to the stomach and duodenum and carries vessels to the liver. Pick it for the fold between the liver and the stomach, not the body wall.
The mesentery is the fan-shaped fold binding the jejunum and ileum to the posterior abdominal wall. It would be the answer for the fold that holds the small intestine.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: A single large duct from each side opens on a small bump right beside the lingual frenulum, under the tongue. Which gland does it drain?
options: The submandibular gland
A minor labial gland
The sublingual gland
The parotid gland
questions.why: The submandibular glands lie along the inner side of the mandible, and each has one main duct that runs forward under the tongue to open near the lingual frenulum, the midline fold that anchors the tongue. The sublingual glands, by contrast, drain through several small ducts spread along the floor of the mouth. One large duct beside the frenulum points to the submandibular gland.
notes: Correct. Each submandibular gland has one main duct that opens on a small bump beside the lingual frenulum.
Minor labial glands are small salivary glands in the lining of the lips with tiny openings of their own. Pick them for the small glands scattered in the lip, not a large paired duct.

The sublingual gland drains through several small ducts spread along the floor of the mouth rather than one large duct beside the frenulum. It would be the answer if the question described many small openings under the tongue.
The parotid duct opens high in the cheek, beside the upper second molar. Pick the parotid if the duct opening were inside the cheek rather than under the tongue.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Where does the parotid duct open into the mouth?
options: On the soft palate near the uvula
Beside the upper second molar
Along the floor of the mouth
Beside the lingual frenulum
questions.why: The parotid gland sits in front of and below the ear, outside the mouth. Its duct runs forward across the masseter muscle, turns inward through the cheek, and opens on the inside of the cheek beside the upper second molar. You can feel the small bump of this opening with your tongue.
notes: No large salivary duct opens on the soft palate. Only small minor palatal glands open there, so this would fit a question about minor salivary glands.
Correct. The parotid duct crosses the masseter, passes through the buccinator, and opens inside the cheek beside the upper second molar.
The floor of the mouth is where the sublingual glands drain through several small ducts. It would be the answer for the sublingual glands.
The openings beside the lingual frenulum belong to the submandibular ducts. Pick this location for the submandibular glands.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Why are the teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas called accessory organs rather than parts of the alimentary canal?
options: None of them makes contact with food at any point
They all release hormones into the blood instead of secretions into ducts
They are not part of the tube that food travels through, though they help digestion
They all lie outside the abdominopelvic cavity
questions.why: The alimentary canal is the continuous tube from the mouth to the anus that food actually travels through. The accessory organs help digestion without being part of that tube. The teeth and tongue work on food in the mouth, and the salivary glands, liver, and pancreas add secretions to the canal through ducts, with the gallbladder storing bile along the way.
notes: The teeth and tongue make direct contact with food in the mouth, so this is false. Students pick it by focusing only on the glands, which add secretions without touching the food directly.

Most accessory organs release their products through ducts, which makes them exocrine. Only the pancreatic islets release hormones into the blood, so this describes endocrine tissue, not the accessory organs as a group.
Correct. Food never passes through these organs; they help digestion from beside the tube.
The liver, gallbladder, and pancreas all sit inside the abdominopelvic cavity. Only the teeth, tongue, and salivary glands lie in the head, so location does not separate the two groups.
questions.answerText: They are not part of the tube that food travels through, though they help digestion

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The liver, salivary glands, and pancreas release their digestive secretions through ducts onto the lining of the digestive tract. This makes them which kind of gland?
options: Lymphatic organs
Exocrine glands
Endocrine glands
Storage organs
questions.why: Exocrine glands (exo means outward) release their products through ducts onto a surface, such as the lining of the mouth or the duodenum. Saliva, bile, and pancreatic juice all reach the digestive tract this way. Endocrine glands, by contrast, have no ducts and release hormones into the blood.
notes: Lymphatic organs, such as lymph nodes, the spleen, and the thymus, house immune cells and filter lymph or blood. They would fit a question about immune defense, not digestive secretions.
Correct. Exocrine glands release their products through ducts onto a surface, which is how saliva, bile, and pancreatic juice reach the tract.
Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the blood without ducts. Pick this term for the pancreatic islets or the thyroid, not for glands that empty digestive juices through ducts.
A storage organ holds a secretion made somewhere else, which describes the gallbladder. The liver, salivary glands, and pancreas make their own secretions, so they are glands, not storage organs.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The right and left hepatic ducts merge to form which single duct?
options: The common bile duct
The common hepatic duct
The main pancreatic duct
The cystic duct
questions.why: The right and left hepatic ducts drain bile from the two halves of the liver and merge just outside the liver into the common hepatic duct. The common hepatic duct is then joined by the cystic duct from the gallbladder, and only below that junction is the duct called the common bile duct. Follow the names in order: hepatic, then common hepatic, then common bile.
notes: The common bile duct forms one step later, where the common hepatic duct meets the cystic duct. Pick it for the duct formed by those two, not by the hepatic ducts alone.
Correct. The two hepatic ducts merge just outside the liver into the single common hepatic duct.
The main pancreatic duct drains pancreatic juice and has nothing to do with the hepatic ducts until it meets the common bile duct at the ampulla. Pick it for the duct of Wirsung.
The cystic duct connects the gallbladder to the duct system. It would be the answer for the duct that carries bile to and from the gallbladder.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The pancreatic islets are also known by which name?
options: The acini
The islets of Langerhans
The hepatic laminae
The portal triads
questions.why: The pancreatic islets, also called the islets of Langerhans, are small clusters of endocrine cells scattered among the much more numerous acini. They make up only about 1 percent of the pancreas and release hormones into the blood. The name islets fits because they look like little islands surrounded by a sea of acini.
notes: The acini are the exocrine clusters of the pancreas that make pancreatic juice, about 99 percent of the gland. They are the sea around the islets, not another name for them.
Correct. The pancreatic islets are the islets of Langerhans.
Hepatic laminae are the plates of hepatocytes in the liver. They would be the answer for how liver cells are arranged, not for pancreatic tissue.
Portal triads are the bile duct, hepatic artery branch, and portal vein branch at the corners of liver lobules. Pick them for a question about liver lobule structure.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which structure on the underside of the liver serves as the gateway where vessels and ducts enter and leave the liver?
options: The renal hilum
The falciform ligament
The major duodenal papilla
The porta hepatis
questions.why: Porta means door, and the porta hepatis is the doorway on the inferior surface of the liver. The hepatic portal vein and hepatic artery enter here, and the hepatic ducts carry bile out. Many organs have a similar gateway, but each has its own name.
notes: The renal hilum is the indented gateway on the medial side of the kidney where the renal vessels and ureter enter and leave. It would be the answer for the kidney's equivalent of the porta hepatis.
The falciform ligament is a fold of peritoneum on the anterior surface that attaches the liver to the abdominal wall and diaphragm. Pick it for the ligament between the right and left lobes.
The major duodenal papilla is the raised opening in the duodenum where bile and pancreatic juice enter. It is a gateway into the intestine, not into the liver.
Correct. Porta means door, and the porta hepatis is where the portal vein and hepatic artery enter and the hepatic ducts leave.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The pancreas is called a mixed gland. Which pair of tissues makes it mixed?
options: Endocrine islets that make hormones and a sac that stores bile
Lymphatic follicles that trap microbes and acini that make digestive juice
Exocrine acini that make digestive juice and endocrine islets that make hormones
Hepatocytes that make bile and sinusoids that carry blood
questions.why: The pancreas does two jobs with two kinds of tissue. About 99 percent of it is exocrine acini, which make pancreatic juice and send it through ducts to the duodenum. The other 1 percent is endocrine pancreatic islets, which release hormones directly into the blood, and having both kinds is what makes it a mixed gland.
notes: The pancreas does have endocrine islets, but the sac that stores bile is the gallbladder, a separate organ. This pair mixes the pancreas with the gallbladder.
Lymphatic follicles are clusters of immune cells found in places like the appendix and tonsils, not a main tissue of the pancreas. Only the acini part of this pair belongs to the pancreas.
Correct. Exocrine acini plus endocrine islets make the pancreas a mixed gland.
Hepatocytes and sinusoids are the cells and blood channels of the liver. Pick this pair for a question about liver histology.
questions.answerText: Exocrine acini that make digestive juice and endocrine islets that make hormones

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which two lobes make up most of the liver?
options: The caudate and quadrate lobes
The right and left lobes
The anterior and posterior lobes
The superior and inferior lobes
questions.why: The right and left lobes are the two principal lobes of the liver, and the right lobe is the larger of the two. The falciform ligament marks the boundary between them on the anterior surface. The caudate and quadrate lobes are two much smaller lobes seen only on the posterior and inferior surface.
notes: The caudate and quadrate lobes are real liver lobes, but they are the two small ones on the posterior and inferior surface. Pick them if the question asked for the small lobes.
Correct. The right and left lobes are the two large lobes seen from the front, and the right lobe is the largest.
Anterior and posterior lobes describe the pituitary gland, not the liver. Pick this pair for a question about the two parts of the pituitary.
Superior and inferior lobes are lobes of the lungs, such as the two lobes of the left lung. They would be the answer for a lung question, not the liver.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The head, body, and tail are the three regions of which accessory organ?
options: The liver
The parotid gland
The pancreas
The gallbladder
questions.why: The pancreas is divided into a head, body, and tail. The wide head sits in the C-shaped curve of the duodenum, the body crosses behind the stomach, and the tapered tail reaches toward the spleen. Picture it lying sideways across the upper abdomen with its head on the right.
notes: The liver is divided into lobes (right, left, quadrate, and caudate), not a head, body, and tail. Pick it for a question about lobes.
The parotid gland is a salivary gland in front of the ear and is not divided into named regions in this course. It would be the answer for the largest salivary gland.
Correct. The pancreas has a head, body, and tail.
The gallbladder has a fundus, body, and neck. The shared word body makes this an easy mix-up, so remember that the gallbladder ends in a neck rather than a head and tail.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Mumps is a viral infection best known for swelling which glands?
options: The palatine tonsils
The gallbladder
The liver
The parotid glands
questions.why: Mumps is a viral infection that inflames and enlarges the parotid glands, the largest salivary glands, which sit in front of and below each ear. Because the parotids lie over the angle of the jaw, the swelling gives the face a puffy look below the ears. Each accessory organ disorder is easiest to remember by the structure it affects.
notes: The palatine tonsils are lymphatic tissue in the throat, and their swelling is tonsillitis. Students pick them because both conditions cause swelling near the jaw, but tonsils sit inside the throat, not in front of the ear.
Mumps does not affect the gallbladder. Inflammation of the gallbladder is cholecystitis, often from a blocking gallstone.
Mumps does not affect the liver. Inflammation of the liver, usually from a virus, is hepatitis, so pick the liver for hepatitis or cirrhosis.
Correct. The mumps virus infects the parotid glands, so the face swells in front of and below the ears.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Between meals, bile flows into the gallbladder for storage, and during a meal it flows back out the same way. Which duct carries bile both into and out of the gallbladder?
options: The common hepatic duct
The cystic duct
The common bile duct
The main pancreatic duct
questions.why: The gallbladder has only one duct, the cystic duct, which joins the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct. When the sphincter of Oddi is closed between meals, bile backs up the cystic duct into the gallbladder for storage. When a fatty meal arrives, the gallbladder contracts and sends bile back down the same cystic duct into the common bile duct.
notes: The common hepatic duct carries bile one way only, out of the liver toward the junction with the cystic duct. Pick it for the duct formed by the right and left hepatic ducts.
Correct. The cystic duct carries bile into and out of the gallbladder.
Bile reaches the gallbladder from the common hepatic duct by way of the cystic duct. The common bile duct carries bile on down to the duodenum, so it is not the gallbladder's way in and out.
The main pancreatic duct carries pancreatic juice, not bile, from the pancreas to the ampulla. Pick it for the duct of Wirsung.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which duct forms where the common hepatic duct and the cystic duct join?
options: The main pancreatic duct
The common bile duct
The right hepatic duct
The hepatopancreatic ampulla
questions.why: The common hepatic duct brings bile down from the liver, and the cystic duct connects to the gallbladder. Where these two meet, the single duct that continues downward is the common bile duct. It runs behind the duodenum and through the head of the pancreas to meet the main pancreatic duct.
notes: The main pancreatic duct drains the pancreas and meets the common bile duct farther down. It would be the answer for the duct of Wirsung.
Correct. The common hepatic and cystic ducts form the common bile duct.
The right hepatic duct drains bile from the right side of the liver and lies upstream of this junction. Pick it for one of the two ducts that form the common hepatic duct.
The hepatopancreatic ampulla is the short widened passage where the common bile duct and pancreatic duct meet, downstream of this junction. Pick it for where bile and pancreatic juice combine.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: What is the short, widened passage where the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct meet just before the duodenum?
options: The cystic duct
The major duodenal papilla
The porta hepatis
The hepatopancreatic ampulla
questions.why: An ampulla is a widened section of a duct. The hepatopancreatic ampulla gets its name from the two ducts it joins, hepato for the bile duct from the liver and pancreatic for the pancreatic duct. It empties into the duodenum through the major duodenal papilla, with the sphincter of Oddi controlling the flow.
notes: The cystic duct connects the gallbladder to the bile duct system, far upstream of the duodenum. It would be the answer for the duct that carries bile to and from the gallbladder.
The major duodenal papilla is the raised opening on the duodenal lining where the ampulla empties. It is the exit of the ampulla, so pick it for the opening into the duodenum.
The porta hepatis is the gateway on the underside of the liver where vessels enter and the hepatic ducts leave. Pick it for the doorway into the liver.
Correct. The hepatopancreatic ampulla is the short widened chamber in the duodenal wall where the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct meet.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: An accessory organ is a soft, tapering gland whose head sits in the curve of the duodenum and whose tail reaches toward the spleen. Which organ is it?
options: The gallbladder
The spleen
The pancreas
The liver
questions.why: The pancreas lies behind the stomach in a retroperitoneal position. Its wide head nestles in the C-shaped curve of the duodenum, its body crosses the posterior abdominal wall, and its tapered tail ends near the spleen. Those landmarks at each end are the quickest way to recognize it on a model.
notes: The gallbladder is a small pear-shaped sac on the posterior surface of the liver, with a fundus, body, and neck. It would be the answer for the organ that stores bile.
The spleen is the lymphatic organ the tail of the pancreas points toward, not the organ described. Pick it for the organ in the left upper quadrant that filters blood.
Correct. The pancreas has its head in the duodenal curve and its tail by the spleen.
The liver sits in the right upper quadrant under the diaphragm and is divided into lobes, not a head and tail. Pick it for the largest gland in the body.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: A patient has inflammation of the liver caused by a viral infection. Which disorder is this?
options: Hepatitis
Cholecystitis
Cirrhosis
Pancreatitis
questions.why: The suffix itis means inflammation, and hepat refers to the liver, so hepatitis is inflammation of the liver. It is most commonly caused by a viral infection. Reading the root of each disorder name tells you which accessory organ is affected.
notes: Correct. Hepat means liver and itis means inflammation, so viral inflammation of the liver is hepatitis.
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder (chole means bile, cyst means bladder). It would be the answer if the gallbladder were inflamed.
Cirrhosis is the replacement of healthy liver tissue with scar tissue after long-term damage, not an inflammation. Pick it for scarring with loss of liver function.
Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas. Pick it if the inflamed organ were the pancreas, for example after a gallstone blocks the ampulla.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which disorder replaces healthy liver tissue with scar tissue, with a loss of liver function?
options: Hepatitis
Cirrhosis
Jaundice
Cholecystitis
questions.why: Cirrhosis develops after long-term damage to the liver. Healthy hepatocytes are gradually replaced by scar tissue, which hardens the liver and leaves fewer working cells, so liver function is lost. It differs from hepatitis, which is inflammation, though repeated inflammation can eventually lead to cirrhosis.
notes: Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver, commonly viral. Pick it for an inflamed liver rather than a scarred one.
Correct. Cirrhosis is scarring of the liver with loss of function.
Jaundice is yellowing of the skin and eyes from a buildup of bilirubin. It is a sign that can accompany liver disease, so pick it for the yellow color, not the scarring.
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder, often from a blocking gallstone. It would be the answer for an inflamed gallbladder.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which salivary glands lie in the floor of the mouth along the inner side of the mandible?
options: The parotid glands
The buccal glands
The sublingual glands
The submandibular glands
questions.why: Sub means below and mandibular refers to the mandible, so the submandibular glands sit just below and inside the body of the mandible, in the floor of the mouth. Their ducts run forward to open near the lingual frenulum. You can feel them as soft lumps under the jaw on each side.
notes: The parotid glands sit in front of and below the ears, outside the mouth over the masseter. Pick them for the largest salivary gland.
The buccal glands are minor salivary glands scattered in the lining of the cheek. Pick them for the small glands of the cheek wall.
The sublingual glands lie beneath the tongue, just above the submandibular glands. They would be the answer for the glands directly under the tongue.
Correct. The submandibular glands lie along the inner mandible.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which disorder is inflammation of the gallbladder, often caused by a blocking gallstone?
options: Hepatitis
Cholecystitis
Cirrhosis
Pancreatitis
questions.why: The name breaks down into chole (bile), cyst (bladder or sac), and itis (inflammation), so cholecystitis is inflammation of the bile sac, the gallbladder. A gallstone blocking the cystic duct traps bile inside the gallbladder, which often triggers the inflammation. Pain is felt in the right upper quadrant.
notes: Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver, commonly viral. It would be the answer for an inflamed liver, not the gallbladder.
Correct. Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder.
Cirrhosis is scarring of the liver with loss of function after long-term damage. Pick it for a scarred, hardened liver.
Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas. A gallstone can cause it too, but only when the stone blocks the shared ampulla, so pick it when the pancreas is the inflamed organ.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which exocrine clusters of the pancreas produce pancreatic juice rich in digestive enzymes?
options: The pancreatic islets
The hepatocytes
The liver lobules
The acini
questions.why: Acini (singular acinus, from the Latin for grape) are berry-like clusters of secretory cells that make up about 99 percent of the pancreas. They produce pancreatic juice, which drains through small ducts into the pancreatic ducts and on to the duodenum. Because they secrete through ducts, they are the exocrine part of the gland.
notes: The pancreatic islets are the endocrine clusters that release hormones into the blood, about 1 percent of the gland. Pick them for the hormone-producing part of the pancreas.
Hepatocytes are the functional cells of the liver, which make bile. They would be the answer for the liver's main cell type.
Liver lobules are the small hexagonal units of the liver. Pick them for the building blocks of the liver, not the pancreas.
Correct. The acini make pancreatic juice.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Hardened deposits that form from bile and can lodge in and block the bile ducts are called what?
options: Jaundice
Gallstones
Cholecystitis
Kidney stones
questions.why: Gallstones are hardened deposits that form in the gallbladder from components of bile. A stone can slip into the cystic duct, the common bile duct, or the hepatopancreatic ampulla and block the flow of bile. That blockage is behind several other disorders, including cholecystitis, jaundice, and pancreatitis.
notes: Jaundice is yellowing of the skin and eyes from a buildup of bilirubin, which can follow a blocked bile duct. It is a sign, not a deposit.
Correct. Gallstones are hardened bile deposits.
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder, which a gallstone often causes. It is the result of the blockage, not the deposit itself.
Kidney stones are hardened deposits that form in the urinary system and can block a ureter. Pick them for a stone that blocks the flow of urine, not bile.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the roles of the liver and the gallbladder in handling bile?
options: The liver makes bile, and the gallbladder stores and concentrates it
Both organs make bile, but only the gallbladder releases it into the duodenum
The liver makes bile, and the gallbladder adds digestive enzymes to it
The gallbladder makes bile, and the liver stores and concentrates it
questions.why: Hepatocytes in the liver produce bile continuously. Between meals, much of that bile backs up the cystic duct into the gallbladder, which stores it and concentrates it by removing water. When a fatty meal arrives, the gallbladder contracts and sends a concentrated supply down to the duodenum.
notes: Correct. The liver produces bile and the gallbladder stores and concentrates it.
Only the liver makes bile, and bile reaches the duodenum whether it comes straight from the liver or from storage. Students choose this when they assume any organ holding bile must also produce it.
Bile contains no digestive enzymes, and the gallbladder adds none. Digestive enzymes come from the pancreas, so pick the pancreas for the organ that supplies enzymes to the duodenum.
This reverses the two roles. The liver is the gland that makes bile, and the gallbladder is the storage sac, which is why the notes classify the gallbladder as a storage organ.
questions.answerText: The liver makes bile, and the gallbladder stores and concentrates it

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which salivary glands sit in the floor of the mouth beneath the tongue and drain through several small ducts?
options: The buccal glands
The submandibular glands
The sublingual glands
The parotid glands
questions.why: Sub means below and lingual means tongue, so the sublingual glands sit directly beneath the tongue, above the submandibular glands. Unlike the parotid and submandibular glands, which each drain through one main duct, the sublingual glands drain through several small ducts that open onto the floor of the mouth. They are the smallest of the three large pairs.
notes: The buccal glands are minor salivary glands in the lining of the cheek. Pick them for the small glands of the cheek wall.

The submandibular glands lie along the inner side of the mandible, below the sublingual glands, and each drains through one main duct near the lingual frenulum. They would be the answer for a single duct beside the frenulum.
Correct. The sublingual glands lie beneath the tongue and use several small ducts.
The parotid glands sit in front of and below the ears and drain through one duct that opens beside the upper second molar. Pick them for the largest salivary gland.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which sequence traces bile from the liver to the gallbladder for storage between meals?
options: Liver, hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct, cystic duct, gallbladder
Liver, hepatic ducts, common bile duct, cystic duct, gallbladder
Liver, hepatic ducts, main pancreatic duct, cystic duct, gallbladder
Liver, common bile duct, hepatic ducts, gallbladder
questions.why: Bile leaves the liver through the right and left hepatic ducts, which merge into the common hepatic duct. When the sphincter of Oddi is closed between meals, bile cannot enter the duodenum, so it backs up and flows through the cystic duct into the gallbladder. The cystic duct branches off where the common hepatic duct becomes the common bile duct, so bile turns up into the gallbladder at that junction.
notes: Correct. Bile leaves through the hepatic ducts and the common hepatic duct, then turns up the cystic duct into the gallbladder.
This route skips the common hepatic duct, where the right and left hepatic ducts merge. Bile cannot reach the cystic duct without passing through the common hepatic duct first.

The main pancreatic duct carries pancreatic juice from the pancreas, not bile from the liver, and it does not connect to the cystic duct. Pick it for the duct that joins the common bile duct at the ampulla.
The hepatic ducts come first, right at the liver, and the common bile duct forms later. This sequence puts the downstream duct before the upstream ones.
questions.answerText: Liver, hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct, cystic duct, gallbladder

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: During a fatty meal, which sequence traces bile from the gallbladder to the duodenum?
options: Gallbladder, cystic duct, common bile duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, duodenum
Gallbladder, cystic duct, main pancreatic duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, duodenum
Gallbladder, common hepatic duct, common bile duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, duodenum
Gallbladder, common bile duct, cystic duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, duodenum
questions.why: The gallbladder contracts and pushes bile out through its only exit, the cystic duct. The cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct, which carries bile down to the hepatopancreatic ampulla. From the ampulla, bile passes the sphincter of Oddi and enters the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla.
notes: Correct. Bile leaves through the cystic duct, runs down the common bile duct to the ampulla, and then enters the duodenum.
Bile does not travel through the main pancreatic duct. That duct carries pancreatic juice and meets the common bile duct only at the ampulla.
The common hepatic duct brings bile down from the liver and is upstream of the gallbladder's junction. Bile leaving the gallbladder never flows up into it, so pick it for the route out of the liver.
The cystic duct comes first because it is the gallbladder's own duct. The common bile duct only forms after the cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct.
questions.answerText: Gallbladder, cystic duct, common bile duct, hepatopancreatic ampulla, duodenum

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: A drop of bile is made in the liver, stored in the gallbladder overnight, and released into the duodenum at breakfast. Which duct does it pass through twice, once in each direction?
options: The common hepatic duct
The cystic duct
The main pancreatic duct
The common bile duct
questions.why: The full route is liver, hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct, then up the cystic duct into the gallbladder. At breakfast the gallbladder contracts, and the bile goes back down the same cystic duct, into the common bile duct, through the hepatopancreatic ampulla, and into the duodenum. The cystic duct is the gallbladder's only connection, so stored bile must use it both ways.
notes: The common hepatic duct is used only once, on the way out of the liver. Pick it for the duct formed by the right and left hepatic ducts.
Correct. The cystic duct carries bile into the gallbladder and back out.
The main pancreatic duct carries pancreatic juice, and bile never travels through it. Pick it for the duct of Wirsung that joins the common bile duct.
The common bile duct carries the drop on its final trip down to the ampulla. The gallbladder's own two-way connection is the cystic duct, not the common bile duct.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: A small gallstone lodges at the hepatopancreatic ampulla. Which two ducts can it block at the same time?
options: The right and left hepatic ducts
The common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct
The cystic duct and the common hepatic duct
The accessory pancreatic duct and the cystic duct
questions.why: The hepatopancreatic ampulla is where the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct meet before opening into the duodenum. A stone stuck there blocks the shared passage, so neither bile nor pancreatic juice can drain. This shared anatomy is why a gallstone can cause pancreatitis as well as jaundice.
notes: The right and left hepatic ducts are near the liver, far upstream of the ampulla. They would be the answer for the ducts that merge into the common hepatic duct.
Correct. The common bile duct and main pancreatic duct share the ampulla.
The cystic and common hepatic ducts meet higher up, at the start of the common bile duct, well above the ampulla. Pick this pair if the stone were stuck where those two ducts join.
The accessory pancreatic duct empties into the duodenum separately and does not pass through the ampulla, and the cystic duct is far upstream. A stone at the ampulla would leave both of these open.
questions.answerText: The common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which set correctly pairs the liver, the pancreas, and the gallbladder with the way each organ is subdivided?
options: Liver into cardia, body, and pylorus, pancreas into head, body, and tail, gallbladder into lobes
Liver into lobes, pancreas into fundus, body, and neck, gallbladder into head, body, and tail
Liver into lobes, pancreas into head, body, and tail, gallbladder into fundus, body, and neck
Liver into head, body, and tail, pancreas into lobes, gallbladder into fundus, body, and neck
questions.why: The liver is divided into lobes: the large right and left lobes plus the small quadrate and caudate lobes. The pancreas runs from a head in the curve of the duodenum through a body to a tail near the spleen. The gallbladder has a rounded fundus, a middle body, and a narrow neck that leads into the cystic duct.
notes: Cardia, body, and pylorus are regions of the stomach, not the liver, and the gallbladder has no lobes. Only the pancreas is subdivided correctly in this set.
This swaps the pancreas and gallbladder. The gallbladder is the one with a fundus and neck, and the pancreas has the head and tail; only the liver is correct here.
Correct. Lobes for the liver, head, body, and tail for the pancreas, and fundus, body, and neck for the gallbladder.
This swaps the liver and pancreas. The pancreas is the organ with a head, body, and tail, while the liver is divided into lobes; only the gallbladder is correct here.
questions.answerText: Liver into lobes, pancreas into head, body, and tail, gallbladder into fundus, body, and neck

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which accessory organ lies in the right upper quadrant, drains its secretion through the right and left hepatic ducts, and has a storage sac attached to its posterior surface?
options: The liver
The gallbladder
The duodenum
The pancreas
questions.why: Every clue points to the liver. It sits under the diaphragm mostly in the right upper quadrant, its bile drains out through the right and left hepatic ducts, and the gallbladder, which stores that bile, is attached to its posterior surface. Putting several clues together like this is how you confirm a structure on a model.
notes: Correct. The liver sits mostly in the right upper quadrant, drains bile through the right and left hepatic ducts, and has the gallbladder on its underside.
The gallbladder is the storage sac in the question, not the organ it is attached to. It would be the answer for the organ that stores and concentrates bile.
The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine, part of the alimentary canal rather than an accessory organ. Pick it for where bile and pancreatic juice are delivered.
The pancreas lies behind the stomach and drains pancreatic juice through the pancreatic ducts, not the hepatic ducts. Pick it for the gland with a head in the curve of the duodenum.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which list names the six accessory digestive organs?
options: Mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine
Teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and appendix
Teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas
Liver, spleen, pancreas, stomach, duodenum, and colon
questions.why: The six accessory digestive organs are the teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas. The teeth and tongue work on food directly in the mouth, the salivary glands, liver, and pancreas add secretions through ducts, and the gallbladder stores bile. None of them is part of the tube that food travels through.
notes: This is the alimentary canal, the tube food actually passes through from mouth to anus. Pick this list for the organs of the digestive tract itself.
This list is close, but it swaps the pancreas for the appendix. The appendix hangs from the cecum and is part of the large intestine, while the pancreas is the accessory organ that belongs here.
Correct. These six help digestion without being part of the tube that food travels through.
This list mixes the spleen, a lymphatic organ, and canal organs such as the stomach, duodenum, and colon in with two accessory organs. It would not match either group cleanly.
questions.answerText: Teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Most accessory organs are glands that make a secretion. Which accessory organ is classified as a storage organ instead, because it holds a secretion made somewhere else?
options: The gallbladder
The liver
The pancreas
The parotid gland
questions.why: The glandular accessory organs, the salivary glands, liver, and pancreas, each produce their own secretion and deliver it through ducts. The gallbladder produces no secretion of its own. It stores bile made by the liver and concentrates it until a meal arrives, so the notes classify it as a storage organ.
notes: Correct. The gallbladder stores bile made by the liver.
The liver is a gland that makes bile, the very secretion the storage organ holds. Pick it for the organ that produces bile.
The pancreas is a gland that makes its own pancreatic juice and hormones. It would be the answer for the accessory organ that is both exocrine and endocrine.
The parotid gland makes its own saliva and delivers it through the parotid duct. Pick it for the largest salivary gland.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which salivary glands lie anterior and inferior to the ears, between the skin and the masseter muscle?
options: The lingual glands
The parotid glands
The sublingual glands
The submandibular glands
questions.why: Para means beside and otic refers to the ear, so the parotid glands sit beside the ear, anterior and inferior to it, lying over the masseter muscle just under the skin. They are the largest salivary glands. Their ducts cross the masseter and open inside the cheek beside the upper second molar.
notes: The lingual glands are small glands within the tongue that secrete mucus and watery fluid. Pick them for glands inside the tongue itself.
Correct. The parotid glands lie in front of and below the ears.
The sublingual glands lie beneath the tongue in the floor of the mouth. They would be the answer for the glands directly under the tongue.
The submandibular glands lie in the floor of the mouth along the inner side of the mandible. Pick them for the glands under the jaw whose ducts open near the frenulum.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The sublingual glands sit beneath the tongue. Which other pair of salivary glands lies just below them?
options: The lingual glands
The parotid glands
The buccal glands
The submandibular glands
questions.why: In the floor of the mouth, the salivary glands are stacked. The sublingual glands lie just beneath the tongue, and the submandibular glands sit below them, along the inner side of the mandible. The parotid glands are separate, out by the ears.
notes: The lingual glands are small glands within the tongue itself, above the floor of the mouth. Pick them for glands that secrete inside the tongue.
The parotid glands sit in front of and below the ears, outside the floor of the mouth. Pick them for the glands over the masseter muscle.
The buccal glands are minor salivary glands in the lining of the cheeks. They would be the answer for small glands scattered in the cheek wall.
Correct. The submandibular glands lie below the sublingual glands.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which digestive secretion does the liver produce?
options: Insulin
Saliva
Pancreatic juice
Bile
questions.why: The liver is the largest gland in the body, and its digestive product is bile. Hepatocytes make bile and release it into the bile canaliculi, which drain into the hepatic ducts. The gallbladder stores the bile, but it is the liver that makes it.
notes: Insulin is a hormone released by the pancreatic islets into the blood. Pick it for an endocrine product of the pancreas, not a product of the liver.
Saliva is made by the salivary glands, mainly the parotid, submandibular, and sublingual pairs. Pick saliva for a question about the glands that drain into the mouth.
Pancreatic juice is made by the acini of the pancreas and delivered to the duodenum. It would be the answer for the exocrine product of the pancreas.
Correct. The liver produces bile.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: On the anterior surface of the liver, which structure marks the boundary between the right and left lobes?
options: The mesentery
The greater omentum
The porta hepatis
The falciform ligament
questions.why: The falciform ligament is a thin fold of peritoneum that runs from the anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm onto the front of the liver. Where it attaches, it divides the large right lobe from the smaller left lobe. On a model, find the thin vertical sheet on the front of the liver and you have found the dividing line.
notes: The mesentery is the fan-shaped fold that binds the jejunum and ileum to the posterior abdominal wall. It would be the answer for the fold that holds the small intestine.
The greater omentum is the fatty apron of peritoneum that hangs from the stomach over the intestines. Pick it for the largest fold of peritoneum.
The porta hepatis is the gateway on the inferior surface of the liver where vessels and ducts enter and leave. Pick it for the liver's doorway, not the line between the lobes on the front.
Correct. The falciform ligament separates the right and left lobes.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which three structures make up the portal triad at each corner of a liver lobule?
options: The cystic duct, the common bile duct, and the main pancreatic duct
A central vein, a hepatic sinusoid, and a bile canaliculus
A bile duct, a hepatic artery branch, and a hepatic portal vein branch
Three small branches of the hepatic veins that drain the lobule
questions.why: Each liver lobule has a portal triad at its corners. The branch of the hepatic artery and the branch of the hepatic portal vein bring blood into the lobule, and the bile duct carries bile out. Traffic in the triad therefore runs both ways, with blood coming in and bile going out.
notes: These are large ducts outside the liver that carry bile and pancreatic juice toward the duodenum. Pick them for the duct system below the liver, not microscopic lobule structures.

These are all real lobule structures, but they sit inside the lobule, not at its corners. The central vein is at the center, the sinusoids run between the plates, and the canaliculi lie between the cells.
Correct. A bile duct, a hepatic artery branch, and a hepatic portal vein branch.
The hepatic veins carry blood out of the liver to the inferior vena cava, and they begin from the central veins, not the corners of the lobule. Pick them for the vessels that drain the liver.
questions.answerText: A bile duct, a hepatic artery branch, and a hepatic portal vein branch

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Where does the gallbladder sit?
options: Within the curve of the duodenum
Posterior to the stomach
Beside the cecum in the lower right quadrant
On the posterior surface of the liver
questions.why: The gallbladder is a pear-shaped sac tucked against the posterior and inferior surface of the liver, in the right upper quadrant. Its broad fundus often peeks out below the lower edge of the liver. On a model, lift the liver's lower edge and look underneath to find it.
notes: The curve of the duodenum holds the head of the pancreas. It would be the answer for the widest region of the pancreas.
The space posterior to the stomach holds the pancreas. Pick this location for the pancreas, not the gallbladder.
The lower right quadrant beside the cecum is where the appendix hangs. Pick this location for the appendix.
Correct. The gallbladder sits on the posterior surface of the liver.
questions.answerText: On the posterior surface of the liver

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: What are the three regions of the gallbladder?
options: Cortex, medulla, and pelvis
Cardia, body, and pylorus
Fundus, body, and neck
Head, body, and tail
questions.why: The gallbladder has a fundus, a body, and a neck. The fundus is the broad, rounded inferior end, the body is the middle, and the neck is the tapered superior end that continues as the cystic duct. Picturing a pear with its narrow end pointing up toward the liver helps you place each region.
notes: Cortex, medulla, and pelvis are regions of the kidney. Pick this set for a kidney cut in a frontal section.
Cardia, body, and pylorus are regions of the stomach. This set would be the answer for the stomach, which also has its own fundus.
Correct. The gallbladder has a fundus, body, and neck.
Head, body, and tail are the regions of the pancreas. Pick this set for the gland whose head sits in the curve of the duodenum.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which two ducts join to form the common bile duct?
options: The common hepatic duct and the cystic duct
The right and left hepatic ducts
The cystic duct and the main pancreatic duct
The main and accessory pancreatic ducts
questions.why: The common hepatic duct carries bile down from the liver, and the cystic duct connects the gallbladder. Where these two meet, the duct continues as the common bile duct, which carries bile from both sources down toward the duodenum. The pancreatic duct joins later, at the hepatopancreatic ampulla.
notes: Correct. The common hepatic and cystic ducts form the common bile duct.
The right and left hepatic ducts join to form the common hepatic duct, one step earlier. Pick this pair for the formation of the common hepatic duct.
The main pancreatic duct does meet the bile system, but it joins the common bile duct at the ampulla, not the cystic duct. This pair mixes two different junctions.
The main and accessory pancreatic ducts both drain the pancreas, and they do not join to form any bile duct. Pick them for a question about how the pancreas drains.
questions.answerText: The common hepatic duct and the cystic duct

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: The hepatopancreatic ampulla is also known by which name?
options: The ampulla of Vater
The duct of Santorini
The duct of Wirsung
The sphincter of Oddi
questions.why: The hepatopancreatic ampulla, also called the ampulla of Vater, is the short widened passage where the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct meet before emptying into the duodenum. Several structures in this area carry a person's name, so it helps to pair each name with its plain anatomical term. The ampulla is the meeting chamber, and the other names belong to the ducts and the sphincter around it.
notes: Correct. The hepatopancreatic ampulla is the ampulla of Vater.
The duct of Santorini is the accessory pancreatic duct, which empties into the duodenum separately. It would be the answer for the smaller pancreatic duct.
The duct of Wirsung is the main pancreatic duct, one of the two ducts that meet in the ampulla. Pick it for the main pancreatic duct.
The sphincter of Oddi is the ring of muscle that controls flow from the ampulla into the duodenum. Pick it for the muscle at the exit, not the chamber itself.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: What is another name for the main pancreatic duct?
options: The duct of Wirsung
The duct of Santorini
The sphincter of Oddi
The ampulla of Vater
questions.why: The main pancreatic duct is also called the duct of Wirsung. It runs through the length of the pancreas and joins the common bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla. One way to keep the names straight is that only the main duct, Wirsung, joins the bile duct, while Santorini empties on its own.
notes: Correct. The main pancreatic duct is the duct of Wirsung.
The duct of Santorini is the smaller accessory pancreatic duct, which empties separately into the duodenum. Pick it for the accessory duct.

The sphincter of Oddi is the muscular ring controlling flow from the ampulla into the duodenum. It would be the answer for a question about what regulates bile and pancreatic juice entering the duodenum.
The ampulla of Vater is the hepatopancreatic ampulla, where the main pancreatic duct and common bile duct meet. Pick it for the shared chamber, not the duct itself.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes how the pancreas is divided between its two kinds of tissue?
options: The head is made only of acini, and the tail is made only of islets
The tissue is split evenly, with half acini and half islets
About 99 percent is exocrine acini, and about 1 percent is endocrine islets
About 99 percent is endocrine islets, and about 1 percent is exocrine acini
questions.why: Nearly all of the pancreas, about 99 percent, is made of acini, the exocrine clusters that produce pancreatic juice. The pancreatic islets, the endocrine clusters, make up only about 1 percent and are scattered among the acini like small islands. So although the pancreas is famous for its hormones, most of its tissue is devoted to making digestive juice.
notes: The islets are scattered among the acini through the gland rather than collected into one region. Head, body, and tail are regions of location, and acini are found in all of them.
The two tissues are far from equal. Students pick this when they know the pancreas has two jobs and assume each gets half the tissue.
Correct. The acini make up about 99 percent of the gland, and the islets are small scattered patches making up about 1 percent.
This reverses the proportions. The islets are the small scattered islands, about 1 percent, and the acini form the bulk of the gland.
questions.answerText: About 99 percent is exocrine acini, and about 1 percent is endocrine islets

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: What does the sphincter of Oddi control?
options: Flow from the stomach into the duodenum
Flow from the esophagus into the stomach
Flow from the ileum into the cecum
Flow from the ampulla into the duodenum
questions.why: The sphincter of Oddi is a muscular ring around the hepatopancreatic ampulla where it opens at the major duodenal papilla. It controls when bile and pancreatic juice enter the duodenum. When it stays closed between meals, bile backs up the cystic duct into the gallbladder for storage.
notes: Flow from the stomach into the duodenum is controlled by the pyloric sphincter. It would be the answer for the valve at the end of the stomach.
Flow from the esophagus into the stomach is controlled by the lower esophageal sphincter, also called the cardiac sphincter. Pick it for a question about heartburn and reflux.
Flow from the ileum into the cecum is controlled by the ileocecal sphincter, also called the ileocecal valve. Pick it for the junction of the small and large intestines.
Correct. The sphincter of Oddi controls flow from the ampulla into the duodenum.
questions.answerText: Flow from the ampulla into the duodenum

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: Bile is first collected from the hepatocytes by which tiny channels?
options: The right and left hepatic ducts
The bile canaliculi
The cystic duct
The hepatic sinusoids
questions.why: Bile canaliculi (canaliculus means little canal) are tiny channels squeezed between neighboring hepatocytes. They collect the bile as the cells make it and carry it toward the bile ducts at the edges of the lobule. They are the very first step on the path of bile.
notes: The right and left hepatic ducts collect bile later, after it has drained from the canaliculi and the small bile ducts. They would be the answer for the ducts that leave the liver.
Correct. The bile canaliculi collect bile from the hepatocytes.
The cystic duct is far downstream and connects the gallbladder. Pick it for the duct that carries bile to and from storage.
The hepatic sinusoids are wide, leaky capillaries that carry blood between the plates of hepatocytes. Pick them for the blood channels of the lobule.

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: After leaving the bile canaliculi and small bile ducts, bile gathers into which ducts as it exits the liver?
options: The common bile duct
The cystic duct
The right and left hepatic ducts
The main pancreatic duct
questions.why: Bile flows from the canaliculi into small bile ducts and then gathers into the right and left hepatic ducts, which drain the two sides of the liver. These two merge into the common hepatic duct just outside the liver. From there the bile can detour into the gallbladder or continue toward the duodenum.
notes: The common bile duct forms farther along, where the common hepatic duct meets the cystic duct. Pick it for the duct that carries bile down to the ampulla.
The cystic duct is the detour to the gallbladder, after the hepatic ducts have merged. It would be the answer for the duct that carries bile to storage.
Correct. Bile gathers into the right and left hepatic ducts.
The main pancreatic duct carries pancreatic juice and never receives bile from the liver. Pick it for the duct of Wirsung.
questions.answerText: The right and left hepatic ducts

questions.topic: Salivary glands, liver, gallbladder and pancreas
questions.q: A gallstone completely blocks the cystic duct. What happens to the flow of bile?
options: Pancreatic juice can no longer reach the duodenum
Bile can no longer leave the liver by any route
Bile flows backward into the main pancreatic duct
Bile is cut off from the gallbladder but still reaches the duodenum
questions.why: The cystic duct is a side branch that connects only the gallbladder to the duct system.
